- Far part (its sections 3 and 4). Lemma FS, an elementary scaling statement, CONFIRMED by the theory auditor on its explicit
  domain (AT2838): nonzero L2 tests with int |g|^2/(4|X|^2) finite, every positive dilation of a test again a test,
  0 < alpha < 2, r > 0, P >= 0 and exact homogeneous scaling. Let F be a real quadratic form on such a class with
  F(g_l) = l^(-alpha) F(g) for all l > 0, where g_l(X) = l^(-1) g(X/l); with c(g) = F(g)/||g||^2 and w(g) = int
  g^2/(4|X|^2)/||g||^2, the estimate F(g) <= r ||g||^2 + P int g^2/(4|X|^2) holds for every test if and only if
  Gamma(g) = c(g)/w(g)^(alpha/2) <= c*(r, P) = (2r/(2 - alpha)) (P (2 - alpha)/(alpha r))^(alpha/2) for every test
  with c(g) > 0; with P = 0 the estimate for all tests fails as soon as one test has c(g) > 0, and only then, and it
  then fails at the small dilates of that test, not necessarily at the test itself (AT2861). The note applies it as a
  necessary condition to two model forms, C3 (C_vs3) and CF (C_vs2 + C_vs3 at J^q = 1 with W = 2|X|), with grad
  rhobar = |X|^(-alpha) times the sampled far profile and alpha = 1 - 1/c = 0.447611231. The homogeneity is sampled
  to r = 1.6e5 and EXTRAPOLATED beyond; the radius of the critical dilate in the row that decides the plan reading is
  1.2e7 (its section 3.3 (1)). The largest sampled Gamma is 1.5606 for CF and 0.3774 for C3 on S1 tests; halving dx
  changes Gamma by at most 0.019 in the resolution pairs, the finer grid giving the larger value, and the CF values
  still rise with the scale range of the grid. They are lower values for sup Gamma up to the discretization error and
  do not determine it. The application to the true far forms rested in v01 on its section 3.3 (2), that an estimate
  in the true budgets implies at large scale the model estimate with the same (r, P). The theory auditor REFUTES this inference in
  general (AT2839): for 0 <= chi <= 1 with chi = 0 on r <= R and chi = 1 on r >= 2R, the form int chi |X|^(-alpha)
  |g|^2 agrees exactly with the homogeneous form int |X|^(-alpha) |g|^2 outside 2R and is bounded by R^(-alpha)
  ||g||^2 with zero price, while the homogeneous form has no rate-only bound on all dilations; the small dilations
  that cause the failure may lie inside the cutoff. The counterexample concerns the inference, not the IPM forms. A
  conclusion for the actual far form needs a fixed test at a controlled exterior scale and an error below the strict
  margin, which v01 does not supply (AT2840 OPEN). v02 replaces the refuted step by Remark FS-1, which the theory auditor CONFIRMS
  as a conditional statement at one dilate (AT2859): fix a test g with c = c(g) > 0, w = w(g) and (r, P) with P > 0,
  put rho = Gamma(g)/c*(r, P) and let s_0 be the critical point of the proof of Lemma FS, l_0 = 1/s_0; if at the
  single dilate h = g_(l_0) the true form differs from the model by at most delta ||g||^2 and the true price weight
  is at most (1 + eps) int h^2/(4|X|^2), then for rho > 1 and delta + eps P w s_0^2 < r (rho^(2/(2 - alpha)) - 1) the
  true estimate with (r, P) fails at h. At the row that decides the plan reading (CF, r = (A), P = (C); FLOAT) rho =
  1.2010, the margin is about 0.266 (A) against a model form value of about 1.63 (A) per ||g||^2, so with eps = 0 a
  relative form error up to about 16 percent would be allowed, at a dilate of mean |X| about 7.3e6. The bounds this
  needs at that dilate (the coefficient against the model beyond r = 1.6e5, the share of the dilated test inside the
  near cut, eps from J^(-q) against 1, for which the second theory agent's Lemma E (T2_FS1_EPS_v01, below) is CLAIMED, the grid error
  of c(g) and w(g)) do not exist (AT2840, AT2862 OPEN); the theory auditor's notes that W^2 >= 4|X|^2 alone does not give the
  comparison of the price weight with int h^2/(4|X|^2) after J^(-q) (audit_v869).
- Reading (its section 5), for the homogeneous model forms on the whole dilation class and conditional on the
  EXTRAPOLATED homogeneity; by AT2839 it does not transfer to the actual far forms. At the plan of record
  Gamma/c*((A), (C)) = 1.201 for CF: the model C_vs2 + C_vs3 cannot be charged to (A) alone with a price below 2.26 x
  (C); with all of (C) the rate must be at least 1.26 x (A), so part of (B) is needed, at least 0.019 x (B) with all
  of (A) and (C), and at least 0.092 x (B) if it is charged to (B) alone with all of (C) (Gamma/c* = 0.157 with r =
  (B) and P = (C)). C_vs3 alone fits (A) at both tuples on the test family, with a price of at least 4.0e-3 x (C) at
  the plan. At the fallback (A) alone suffices for CF on the test family, with Gamma/c* = 0.226 and a price of at
  least 1.29e-3 x (C). The note's statement that no far C_vs term can be charged to a rate alone (P = 0) holds only
  for the homogeneous models with a positive value on a class closed under all dilations (Lemma FS); for the actual
  far forms, which live beyond the near cut, it is not shown (AT2839, AT2840); v02 and v03 state it in this

  Table (f) charges the far C_vs1, C_vs3 and T_IS to (B) and C_vs2 to no budget; on this model orientation the far
  C_vs2, priced with C_vs3, would need (B) at the plan of record, which is not shown for the actual forms. A joint
  estimate of a sum of far forms of the same degree (the far T_II part has the coefficient atil) has its own Gamma,
  which the note does not compute.

  fa026457049206fd87aa474f2f540f68ce0e8082883d562db07d43886251c93b; notes 13:40Z; CLAIMED, audit requested and not

  price hypothesis eps of Remark FS-1. With W = (1 + 4|X|^2)^(1/2), J = <D>, the price weight Q(f) = ||W^(-1) J^(-q)

(b) The strain identity and the stronger lower of u_3 (AT2564 CONFIRMED; THEORY_NEW_RESULTS version 22, NR-34
Corollary (c)). Let ubar = (-Psi_y, Psi_x) be planar and divergence-free, S = Sym D ubar, and use the nonunitary
transform (d_j -> i zeta_j) and the operator matrix norm. Then |ubarhat(zeta)| = |zeta| |Psihat(zeta)| and
Shat(zeta) = Psihat(zeta) B(zeta) with B real, symmetric, traceless and ||B(zeta)||_op = |zeta|^2/2, so
    u_3 = m_3(ubar) = m_4(Psi) = 2 m_2(S),   m_k(f) = (2 pi)^(-2) int |zeta|^k |fhat(zeta)| d zeta.
If the moments are finite and the inverse formulas hold, ||Delta S(X)||_op <= m_2(S) for every X, and the numerical auditor's exact
origin lower ||Delta S(0)||_op >= 1899576001577/10^12 (AN725; AT2456) gives
    u_3 >= L2 = 2 x 1899576001577/10^12 = 3799152003154/10^12 = 3.799152003154,
a strict lower of 2 ||Delta S(0)||_op (AT2606).
Hypotheses, stated precisely (the first numerics agent's notes 10:41Z, from the referee pass; AT2588 uses the same reading): fhat is a
measurable function away from zeta = 0 with int |zeta|^k |fhat| finite, with no point-supported part, and every
order-k derivative of f tends to zero at infinity. The polynomial Psi = x^3 y shows that the last condition is
needed: its moments vanish and ||Delta S||_op = 6. For the 013 fields the first numerics agent states the decay
D^alpha Psi = O(r^(1 + 1/c - |alpha|)) from the finite atom representation (CLAIMED there, not audited), which
gives these hypotheses for the moments used here.

(d) Lemma TIS-FG (CONFIRMED by the theory auditor under the smoothness and decay, Lemma KER identity and finite Fourier-moment
hypotheses, AT2437; requested in note 93). Put M_S = (2 pi)^(-2) int |zeta|^2 (1 + 2<zeta>^2)
||S^(zeta)||_op d zeta. If M_S is finite, then |T_IS(g)| <= (q/2) M_S ||J^(-1) g||^2 for every test. Proof (plan
section 3): the kernel symbol factor of T_IS is (n(xi) - n(eta))^2 + (p(xi) - p(eta))^2 with p = 1/<.> and
n = 1 - |.|/<.>; |p(xi) - p(eta)| <= |zeta| p(xi) p(eta); n is radial with |n'| = p^3 decreasing, so |n(xi) - n(eta)|
<= |zeta| P^3 with P the larger of p(xi), p(eta), and Peetre's inequality with P <= 1 gives P^3 <= 2^(1/2) <zeta>
p(xi) p(eta); Young's inequality for the kernel ||S^(xi - eta)||_op |zeta|^2 (1 + 2<zeta>^2) acting on p |v^|
finishes it. Consequence: T_IS is paid from (B) alone if M_S <= 0.012125762. This test is sufficient, not equivalent
(AT2441): the exact threshold of the lower-decimal test is 42440167641/3500000000000 (the theory auditor), and that for the
exact free gain is 3413098628099173/281474976710656000 (the first theory agent, exact fractions). Since 1 + 2<zeta>^2 >= 3
and ||Delta S||_op <= M_S/3 pointwise, the test implies sup ||Delta S||_op <= 0.004041921 on the whole plane. At
013 the test fails. The numerical auditor's exact origin jets of the unwindowed Source013 velocity (AN725) give
sup ||Delta S||_op >= 1899576001577/10^12 (a point evaluation, which needs only the admitted smooth source) and, with
finite Fourier moments and valid nonunitary inverse derivative formulas, M_S >= 5698728004731/10^12 (the theory auditor AT2456,
AT2457 CONFIRMED). So (q/2) M_S exceeds the exact free gain, and the unsplit TIS-FG bound cannot be paid from (B)
(AT2458 CONFIRMED). This excludes that sufficient estimate with that budget only. It does not refute the actual T_IS
form, a sharper estimate, a near and far split, H4 or existence (AT2459 OPEN). T_IS therefore needs a split: the far
part by TIS-FG with the moments of (1 - chi) S, the near part by HI' (high part, into (A)) and an NE-lo bound (low
part, into (C)).

(e) A ceiling from Lemma HI' (CONFIRMED by the theory auditor only as a necessary condition for that nonnegative sufficient upper
to fit, AT2439). Lemma HI' of T2_H4_v01 bounds the high-frequency part of T_IS + C_tr at cut mu_r by phi mu_r^(-2)
[(c_tr' + 5q/2) u_3 + tail] ||g||^2, with u_3 = (2 pi)^(-2) int |zeta|^3 |ubar^(zeta)| d zeta and
c_tr' + 5q/2 = 10.67804022 (arb). That loss is paid from (A), so without the tail term it fits only if u_3 <= R(U)
mu_r^2/(phi (c_tr' + 5q/2)). At U = F and the plan of record (4-digit approximations; the theory auditor's
research/h4rest_plan_v01_audit/CORRECTED_DISPLAYS_v01.md gives directed 12-place values, and 8 of the 20 four-digit
entries of the H4REST_PLAN_v01 table lie below the exact ceiling): u_3 <= 0.2817 at mu_r 72, 0.5433 at 100, 2.173 at
200 and 54.33 at 1000 with the regional lower, and 1.891, 3.648, 14.59 and 364.8 at the ceiling. At the certified
(R4) inputs of V21-3 (version 1) these become 0.2707, 0.5222, 2.089 and 52.22 (regional) and 1.880, 3.627, 14.51 and
362.7 (ceiling), again 4-digit approximations (arb values in research/closure_check/hi_r4v01.out of agent the first theory agent;
NEAR_CHECK_v06 section 6); the theory auditor's directed uppers at this tuple are 0.270727716958 (mu_r 72) and 0.522237108330
(mu_r 100) (AT2465). SCREEN_specification_v01 states the U = F values. Since |(e.grad)^3 ubar_k| <= u_3 pointwise, a pointwise
lower of the third derivatives of ubar is a lower of u_3. The numerical auditor's exact origin jets give
u_3 >= L = 1024389316421/10^12 (AN725; AT2457 CONFIRMED, with finite Fourier moments and valid nonunitary inverse
derivative formulas). Hence the HI' bound can fit in R only if mu_r >= (phi K L/R)^(1/2), K = c_tr' + 5q/2 (AT2464
CONFIRMED). At the plan of record and the regional lower this least cut is about 137.3116 at the near tuple of

(d) What the record is and is not. Like the JC record and job 7's record, it is a finite computation on the admitted
source013 interface (S) of V17-1 (i) and a producer record of the first theory agent. It certifies no root by itself (AT2089). By
numerical audit exchange v590, a fresh completed record, its actual execution settings, full interval evidence and an independent source
reconstruction are needed before a slab enters the certified regional inventory. The theory auditor's conditional coverage
calculation (AT2192, AT2193; AT2194 OPEN) shows what complete admitted evidence on these roots together with the 24
capped roots would give: all 128 indices at the closure targets 3/5, 1/4 and 137/125, with 71/500 still open inside
the balanced roots 98, 100, 102 and 104. 71/500 is a joint flag, not a theory target.

(e) The rate budget of the H4 join (H4-COMP; the second theory agent T2_CLOSURE_CHECK_v01 section 4; the first theory agent's note 88; the theory auditor audit_v715).
Write E(g) for the H4 form on the common domain. The principal part contributes -beta_* ||g||^2, where beta_* is the
certified whole-plane matrix rate. The near loss e_up and every other full-L^2 loss eps_rest are terms in ||g||^2; the
far form is absorbed by its J^(-1) gain, which cannot take a positive full-L^2 error. Adding the component forms
gives
    E(g) <= -(beta_* - e_up - eps_rest) ||g||^2 + (P_HF + C_rest) ||h||^2,
so the H4 step at rate b0 needs
    e_up + eps_rest <= beta_* - b0                                                      (reading (ii)).

### V18-1. Proposition JC: the finite annuli J_7 to J_20 of root 127 (the first theory agent research/background_jcells/PROOF.md, SHA256 0d345eb14a3f...; CLAIMED, for review by the theory auditor and the numerical auditor)

(a) Status. Proposition JC is a finite rigorous computation on the admitted source013 interface (S) of V17-1 (i). It
is not a new theorem and changes no status by itself. The theory auditor CONFIRMS its method (AT1991 to AT1993). The numerical
record of (c) is CLAIMED; it is the evidence that AT1994 asks for. The theory auditor's audit of the complete record (audit_v636)
CONFIRMS its complete product coverage and every recorded scalar target on all 14 annuli (AT2074; 640400 exact
checks over 57344 cells) and CONFIRMS that the JC and TC inequalities give the root 127 bounds of (b) when the
recorded cells enclose the source fields (AT2075). It REFUTES the literal attainment wording of PROOF.md (AT2076;
corrected in (b); the correction is CONFIRMED, AT2085). An independent full-source reconstruction of J_8 to J_20 and
the admission of the JC and TC consumer for root 127 are OPEN (AT2077). The annulus J_7 is certified by both
auditors through two independent reconstructions: the theory auditor's (AT2004 to AT2007) and the numerical auditor's independent checker (the numerical auditor
exchange v574: 32 x 256 cells, 2560-bit compilation, 384-bit cells, direct interval Horner in u in place of the
mean-value form; audited by the theory auditor, AT2054 and AT2055; AT2056 OPEN). The coordinator's 04:40Z note allocates the numerical auditor's
checker one run on J_8 to J_20 on core 50 under at most 1800 s. That run (04:44:04Z to 04:55:29Z, 685.2 s) and
its exact recount passed; the numerical auditor publishes the bounds and CONFIRMS them (exchange v588), and the theory auditor CONFIRMS them
after its own exact audit (AT2092, AT2093; AT2094 OPEN). So J_8 to J_20 is certified by both auditors through
the numerical auditor's reconstruction, and root 127 no longer depends on the JC record; that record stays a producer record
under AT2077. On every annulus the numerical auditor's uppers and lowers satisfy all four targets; they differ from the table of
(c) because the enclosures differ.

(b) Statement. Assume (S). For k = 7, ..., 20 let J_k = {2^k - 1 <= |X|^2 <= 2^(k+1) - 1}, that is
s = 1 - t in [2^-(k+1), 2^-k]. Then for every X with 127 <= |X|^2 <= 2^21 - 1 and every angle:
1. M >= (3/5) I; precisely, for the entries of d0 (M - (3/5) I), a >= 275283/500000, b >= 189059/1000000 and
   a b - (1 - z^2) e^2 >= 28661/250000, so d0^2 det(M - (3/5) I) >= 28661/250000;
2. |grad h| <= G_JC = 3115797103/1000000000000 (= 0.003115797103);
3. ||Sym Du||_op <= S_JC = 175205792209/500000000000 (= 0.350411584418).
The largest recorded uppers, which give G_JC and S_JC, both occur in the J_7 record; the field maxima may be
smaller (this corrects "attained" in PROOF.md, see research/background_jcells/ERRATA.md).
With Proposition TC (r^2 >= 2^21 - 1), on all of root 127 (|X|^2 >= 127) and for every angle each bound is the
weaker of the two constants (AT1995): M >= (3/5) I, |grad h| <= 899/10000 (TC's constant; the smaller JC gradient
does not replace it), ||Sym Du||_op <= S_JC = 175205792209/500000000000 (JC's constant; TC's 729/10000 is smaller)
and d0^2 det(M - (3/5) I) >= 949/20000 (TC's constant). All four targets of the joint flag hold on root 127.

(c) Proof outline (the full proof and the reviewer's checklist are in PROOF.md).
- Centered weights. Fix k, put s_c = 3 2^-(k+2) and s = s_c (1 + u), so J_k is u in [-1/3, 1/3]. Each weight is
  s^B (1 + (a - 1) s)^(-d) = c_b (1 + u)^B (1 + g_b u)^(-d) with c_b > 0 and g_b = (a - 1) s_c/(1 + (a - 1) s_c). The
  program asserts |g_b| < 1, so the Taylor coefficients in u are majorized by those of
  (1 - u)^(-B) (1 - |g_b| u)^(-d), whose value at u = 1/3 is closed.
- Numerators. P_bf(1 - s_c - s_c u, z) is expanded exactly in u^i T_l(z), in 2048-bit balls from the exact
  rationals.
- One series per field. For each branch-field the order N_bf is the least of 120, 140, ..., 480 with tail at most
  1e-25 (480 otherwise). The tail is a closed form minus a partial sum of nonnegative terms, enclosed in balls. The
  branch series are summed into one series per field, the rows beyond NE_f are moved into the tail, and R_f is the
  total. The program stops an annulus if some R_f exceeds 1e-6 (TAILMAX). It prints each actual total as a ball that
  contains it, and jc_table.py compares the upper endpoint of every printed ball exactly with 1e-20; the bound is
  read from the totals, not inferred from the lumping threshold.
- Cells. 16 x 256 cells in (u, phi), z = cos phi, cover [-1/3, 1/3] x [0, pi]. On a cell the angular factor is
  enclosed by a Taylor form with the Lagrange remainder and the radial factor by the mean value form, both in
  256-bit balls, plus [-R_f, R_f]. The predicates of (S) are tested on these balls; a failing cell would be split
  into four, up to depth 4.
- Evidence (jcell_cells_v03.py). For every annulus the program writes the settings, the source and script hashes,
  the orders N_bf, NE_f, an outward dyadic upper of R_f over 2^64, the checkpoints and, for each accepted cell, its
  exact endpoints and the outward dyadic endpoints (denominator 2^64) of a, b, a b - (1 - z^2) e^2, |grad h|^2 and
  ||Sym Du||^2. The program then rechecks in exact rational arithmetic, from those endpoints only, that every
  target holds on every cell. The 2^-64 resolution is too coarse for the tails (the record gives only
  R_f <= 2^-64, about 5.4e-20); the tails are read from the printed balls, as above. They enter the proof only
  through the cell enclosures, which contain [-R_f, R_f] before the outward rounding.
- Cover. The program also checks that the cell areas sum to 2/3. Area alone does not show a cover (AT2014). The
  cover follows from the generation (each failing cell is replaced by its four quarters), and jc_table.py checks it
  exactly from the recorded endpoints alone: every recorded cell is a dyadic quarter-subcell, at its recorded depth,
  of one of the 16 x 256 base cells; no recorded cell equals or contains another; and in every base cell the areas
  add up to the area of the base cell. Closed cells with disjoint interiors that fill the area of a closed base cell
  cover it.

### V18-2. Audit outcomes since theory_v17 (AT1915 to AT2097), errata to theory_v17, and the numerical-audit record (numerical audit exchange v523 to v590)

(a) Errata to theory_v17. The theory auditor audited the theory_v17 prefix in audit_v594 (AT1943 to AT1949). Two wording
implications are REFUTED. Neither one refutes a field inequality, and neither changes a status or a decision.
- E-v17-1 (AT1944). V17-1 (h) 3 (B) says to bound a numerator translated to an arc midpoint by sum_k |c_k| rho^k
  with rho the half-diagonal of the arc box. That is wrong in general. The arc midpoint is not the box center, so
  the half-diagonal need not bound |z - midpoint| on the box. The theory auditor's exact witness: on the unit circle, take
  endpoints 24/25 + (7/25) i and i, midpoint 3/5 + (4/5) i and P(z) = z - midpoint. The half-diagonal squared is
  9/25, but |P|^2 = 2/5 at either endpoint. Corrected text: rho is an upper bound for the sup over the box of
  |z - midpoint|, or the expansion is taken at the box center. The diagnostic research/background_band/
  arc_centered.py already uses rho = abs(box - mid).upper(), the correct radius. Its explanation and comment carry
  the wrong word, and its numbers are unchanged. Its fixed-z samples and truncated products are diagnostics; a
  certificate still needs the analytic tail.
- E-v17-2 (AT1945). V17-0 item 3 shortens root 040's balanced gradient upper 0.515120914659 to 0.5151. That
  rounding is inward (the witness 0.51511 lies strictly between the two numbers). Corrected text: |grad h| < 0.515121
  on balanced root 040 (request 161). Root 039's 0.4823 rounds outward and stands.
- E-v17-3 (status, not an error at publication). theory_v17 calls Proposition TC CLAIMED. It was published at
  02:38:36Z, one minute before AT1915 and AT1916 (audit_v585, 02:39:49Z). TC is CONFIRMED (V18-2 (b) 4).

(b) Remark WF (whole-field remainder). Hypotheses:
1. A radial cell [m - H, m + H] of the exact split of numerical audit exchange v463 (research/background_exterior_join/PROOF.md):
   - one of the roots I_j = [j/128, (j+1)/128], j = 98 to 126;
   - or one of the dyadic cells J_k = [1 - 2^-k, 1 - 2^-(k+1)], k = 7 to 23.
2. The radius R = (9/10)(1 - m) and q = H/R. On J_k, q = 10/27; on I_j, q = 10/(9 (255 - 2j)) <= 10/27 (v463;
   AT1744 CONFIRMS the radii and q <= 10/27).
3. For each z in [-1, 1] and each of the 45 branches, g_b(., z) = f_b P_b(., z) is analytic on an open neighbourhood
   of the closed disk |t - m| <= R. Here f_b = (1 - t)^B (a + (1 - a) t)^(-d) uses the principal branches, and the
   disk avoids t = 1 and every t = a/(a - 1) (v463, AT1744).
4. F = sum_b g_b is one of the seven fields, and M_F = sup of |F(t, z)| over |t - m| = R, z in [-1, 1], is finite.

Conclusion. For real t in [m - H, m + H], z in [-1, 1] and N >= 0,

  |F(t, z) - T_N F(t, z)| <= M_F q^(N+1)/(1 - q),

where T_N F = sum_b T_N g_b is the degree-N Taylor polynomial in t at m.

Proof. By hypothesis 3, F(., z) is analytic near the closed disk, so its Taylor coefficients at m satisfy
|c_k(z)| <= M_F R^(-k). For |t - m| <= H the tail of the series is at most sum over k > N of M_F q^k, which is
M_F q^(N+1)/(1 - q). The Taylor polynomial is linear in F, so T_N F = sum_b T_N g_b.

Since M_F <= sum_b M_b, with M_b = sup of |g_b| on the same circle, the bound is never weaker than the per-branch
remainder sum_b M_b q^(N+1)/(1 - q) of numerical audit exchange v460. That one is CONFIRMED as a conditional range under complete
circle and angular bounds (AT1743, AT1748). Remark WF changes only the remainder. The correlated range of T_N F on
each leaf and the scalar tests of the balanced method are unchanged.

What an application needs: a certified upper for M_F, that is an enclosure of sup |sum_b g_b| on the circle. On the
circle the branch terms still cancel (table below), so the branches must be enclosed jointly. One way is a Taylor
model of each product on an arc, with the coefficients summed over b before the modulus is taken.

Hypothesis (S), the admitted source013 interface (the numerical auditor research/source013_background_source/PROOF.md, common-branch
form, and research/source013_background_admission/PROOF.md; archive polynomials.json.gz with SHA256
2e3c649402c72ad50836f41f35c5657f50232a877557a5641038262355fa689d). With z = cos(2 theta), each field
f in {a, b, e, rh, sh, ud, uh} is

  F_f(t, z) = sum over b = 0..44 of (1 - t)^(B_b) (a_b + (1 - a_b) t)^(-d_b) P_bf(t, z),

with the archive's exact B_b >= 0, a_b > 0 (key "scale"), integers d_b >= 0 and rational polynomials P_bf. With
d0 = 1/4 + 3t/4, d0 (M - (3/5) I) = [[a, sin(2 theta) e], [sin(2 theta) e, b]], grad h = (sin(2 theta) sh, rh) and
Sym Du = [[ud, sin(2 theta) uh/2], [sin(2 theta) uh/2, -ud]].

Statement. Assume (S), and let K be 21 or 24. For every X with |X|^2 >= 2^K - 1 (t in [1 - 2^-K, 1)) and every angle:
1. M >= (3/5) I, with a b - (1 - z^2) e^2 >= 0.04745 (K = 21) and >= 0.04764 (K = 24) (LB);
2. |grad h| <= 0.0899 (K = 21) and <= 0.00164 (K = 24) (UB), so below 71/500, 1/4 and 2.00215453;
3. ||Sym Du||_op <= 0.0729 (K = 21) and <= 0.0338 (K = 24) (UB), so below 137/125.

Proof outline (the full proof and the reviewer's checklist are in PROOF.md).
- Exact translation. Every numerator is rewritten in integers as P_bf(1 - s, z) = sum_i x_i(z) s^i, s = 1 - t. The
  row x_0 = P_bf(1, z) is kept in Chebyshev form. The rows i >= 1 are bounded on [-1, 1] by the smaller of their
  Chebyshev and monomial 1-norms, so sup_z |P_bf(1 - s, z) - x_0(z)| <= sum_{i >= 1} m_i s^i. The translations and
  conversions are checked as integer identities at two points each.
- Cells. With u0 = 1824676646553933/8152952920478362, the least positive B, put y = s^u0. The rectangle
  0 <= y <= Y, 0 <= phi <= pi (z = cos phi), with Y a dyadic upper bound of 2^(-K u0), is cut into 16 x 256 cells. On
  a cell, each weight s^B (1 + (a - 1) s)^(-d) is enclosed by its four endpoint products (both factors are positive
  and monotone), and G(phi) = sum_l C_l cos(l phi) by G(p) + G'(p) [-r, r] + [-1, 1] (r^2/2) sum_l l^2 |C_l|.
- Tests. On each cell, the admission predicates are applied to the ball enclosures (arb, 192 bits), with a ball for
  sin^2(phi) in place of the leaf constant s(J). All 4096 cells pass for K = 21 and for K = 24, without subdivision.

Evidence. cells_K21.out and cells_final.out (K = 21, 7.3 s), cells_K24.out (3.4 s); prep_*.out (5 to 13 s per chunk
of branches). At two points a direct exact evaluation from the archive lies inside the enclosure (CHECKPT in
cells_final.out). All at nice 19 on core 41.

What it gives and what it does not.
- K = 21 contains K = 24, so TC covers v463's terminal cell T and the dyadic cells J_21 to J_23. With AT1882 it
  leaves J_7 to J_20 of root 127 (127 <= r^2 <= 2^21 - 1).
- It does not touch t < 1 - 2^-21, the band roots or the inner roots. It is not a balanced trial.
- Exploratory (not part of TC): K = 20 passes the matrix, the strain and the O1 gradient limit but not 1/4
  (|grad h|^2 <= 0.0997 at depth 1, cells_K20.out). The obstacle is the s-term tail of branch 4 (B = 4 u0), whose
  exponent 1 + 4 u0 equals B of branches 9 to 14 exactly. An exact grouping by powers of s across those branches
  might reach smaller K (HEURISTIC). I do not plan it before X9.
- Like AT1882, TC is a finite computation on the admitted source, not a new theorem. Its status is CLAIMED until
  the theory auditor reviews it, and it changes no status by itself.

### V17-2. Audit outcomes since theory_v16 (AT1710 to AT1914), errata to theory_v16, and the numerical-audit record (numerical audit exchange v446 to v522)

(a) Errata to theory_v16. Each corrects a statement of theory_v16 that the theory auditor REFUTES or that a later check overtakes.
None of them changes a status. The planning conclusions of V16-1 are replaced by V17-1.
- E-v16-1 (AT1716; numerical audit exchange v448, research/background_range_floor/PROOF.md). V16-0 and V16-1 (c) say that no angular
  partition at order 16 can pass 1/4 from root 99 on, or the O1 limit from root 102 on. The floor holds for the bare
  correlated interval C = [A - E, V + E] (AT1715, CONFIRMED). But the evaluator returns C intersected with the
  independent branchwise range D, and an intersection can be narrower than E (AT1716's counterexample
  [-1, 1] intersected with [-1/100, 1/100]; the numerical auditor's example (2)). So those sentences hold only on leaves where D
  contains C. They are readings, not consequences of the admitted range, and AT1719 (OPEN) states that no
  source-specific impossibility is established. The predicted remainders of V16-1 (d) are statements about E and

### V16-1. The capped band 98 to 127: why the original records fail, and what Taylor order and radial subdivision each root needs (coordinator 23:14Z items 2(a) and 2(e); planning for X8)

(a) What was computed. All numbers in this item are FLOAT displays or HEURISTIC predictions, and none is a bound. The
inputs are:

  the numerical auditor's AN413 diagnostic (the numerical auditor research/background_taylor_order_diagnostic/verification/result_v01.json);
- the exact owner source polynomials P_b(t, z) of rh and sh (the numerical auditor
  research/source013_background_source/verification/observed_owner_v02/polynomials.json.gz);
- the order-16 remainder bounds recorded by the owners on the capped roots (the second numerics agent worker_g0_v01 and worker_g1_v01
  output, as quoted by the second numerics agent and the numerical auditor).

The scripts are in the first theory agent research/background_band/:
- majorant_float.py: a FLOAT copy of the per-branch remainder majorant of the numerical auditor research/reference_b14s_cover/PROOF.md
  (lines 67 to 76). It reproduces AN413's seven displayed order-32 ratios to the digits shown.
- ratio_table.py and ratio_table2.py: the predicted floors of (d) below, with outputs ratio_table.out and
  ratio_table2.out.
- branch_size.py and branch_sum.py: exact rational evaluation of single branch terms and of their sums, displayed
  in FLOAT.

(b) Cancellation between branches. I evaluated the 45 branch terms f_b P_b of rh and sh exactly at t = 49/64 (root 98)
and t = 7/8 (root 112), z = 0 and z = 1/2:
- the largest single term has modulus 2.8e6 to 9.9e6;
- the full sums are 6.7e-4 to 8.9e-3 in modulus;
- the ratio between the two is 3.1e8 to 5.3e9.

The fields are therefore small (the first numerics agent's sampled maximum of |grad h| is 0.13845), but they are differences of terms
about 1e9 times larger. The largest terms come from the near-pole branches 10 to 14:
- d = 59 or 107, with scales 1/2, 2, 9, 100 and 900;
- branch 14 has its pole at t = 900/899, a distance 1/899 beyond t = 1, which is less than the root width 1/128;
- |P_14| falls from about 1e254 at t = 0.766 to 1e105 at t = 0.992, while f_14 P_14 stays near 1e4.

Every part of the admitted enclosure that bounds branches separately carries this branch magnitude, not the field:
- the Taylor remainder E = sum_b eps_b M_b of the correlated range (the numerical auditor research/radial_slab_cover/PROOF.md lines
  14 to 35), with M_b = max(|L_b|, |U_b|) from the Bernstein-Chebyshev coefficients of P_b;
- the independent range sum_b f_b([l, r]) [L_b, U_b].

This is the mechanism behind the capped records. It is consistent with the factor of more than 108 that the balanced
replay at order 32 gained on root 98 (V15-6 (b) 3).

(c) A floor that angular refinement cannot remove. On a radial root the correlated range of a field is [A - E, V + E],
with A <= V the range of the summed Taylor polynomial on the cell. E does not depend on the angular cell, so every
leaf interval has width at least 2E and m_f >= E. A leaf that contains z = 0 has k_J = 1, so

  m_rh^2 + k_J m_sh^2 >= E_rh^2 + E_sh^2.

If E_rh^2 + E_sh^2 > g^2, the fresh range alone fails the gradient test at g on that leaf for every angular partition.
An intersection with an old containing record can only narrow the range, but the old records on this band are wider
(G from 18.9 to 596, V15-6 (b) 2), so the intersection does not help at present (HEURISTIC).

(d) Predicted floors at other orders and with radial subdivision. Let T_(N,m),b(j) be the majorant of branch b at
order N on the worst of m equal radial sub-cells of root j. Put
q_(N,m)(j) = max over b of T_(N,m),b(j) / T_(16,1),b(j); the predicted floor of E_sh is q_(N,m)(j) E_sh(j).

Two facts make this an upper estimate of the new remainder, provided the recorded remainder is exactly
sum_b T_(16,1),b M_b:
- M_b does not increase under subdivision, because the Bernstein coefficients on a sub-interval are convex
  combinations of the original ones;
- each T_b falls by at least the factor q.

   K_J = max over J of (1 - z^2) and U_J > (((a_L - b_L)/2)^2 + K_J m_e^2)^(1/2), put L_J = (a_L + b_L)/2 - U_J; then
   ell_J = 3/5 + L_J/d bounds lambda_min(M) below on the cell, with d the left endpoint of d0 = (1 + 3t)/4 on the root
   if L_J < 0 and the right endpoint if L_J >= 0. I checked the argument: lowering both diagonal entries subtracts a
   nonnegative diagonal matrix, the smaller eigenvalue of [[a, w], [w, b]] decreases in |w|, and d0 > 0. So (H-a)
   holds on a root with beta = min over J of ell_J whenever that minimum is positive. Also L_J >= 0 exactly when
   a_L >= 0, b_L >= 0 and a_L b_L - K_J m_e^2 >= 0 (up to the rounding in U_J), so ell_J >= 3/5 reproduces the
   admission test at 3/5. This agent had prepared the same statement for THEORY_NEW_RESULTS and does not enter it
   there, since the numerical auditor states and proves it first.

made explicit as below; AT-1485 is OPEN (its premises are not certified). Proposition O1-013 (conditional). Let
rho_* = rho_bar + h_* be the 013 background, h the density correction of the numerical auditor's cover contract
(research/source013_background_cover/PROOF.md in the numerical auditor), and M(X) = (c + 1 + sigma V(X).X/(eta + |X|^2)) I - q Sym
DV(X) + A(X),   q = 21/10, sigma = 1, eta = 1/4, so that M = -N_q of BG-3 at rho_* with r0 = 1/2. Assume: (H-a)
M(X) >= beta I for every X in R^2, for a rational beta > 0 (the matrix component of the global assembly of the numerical auditor's
admission contract; the cover target is beta = 3/5); (H-b) sup_X |grad h(X)| <= G for a certified rational
G < 2.00215453 (BG-2 of the base: beta_0 > 2.00215453, AN-010); (H-c) RC-2 and RC-4 for h_* (the exact-potential class
and the normalized origin of 013, AT-674, AT-675). Then FW-C2-O1Hq-v1 H1 to H5 hold for rho_*, and T1.2 (AT-031) gives
the unique L2 solution k0 of L_* k0 = -F_* with W k0 in H^(21/10), N(k0) <= N(F_*)/beta_1 + C_1 ||F_*||_2 for
0 < beta_1 < min(beta, beta_0 - G) (C_1 finite, not computed), and <X> k0 in C^(1,1/10). Proof. H1 is RC-2. H2 is BG-2
at rho_* with beta_0* = beta_0 - G > 0: on the common generator domain L_* = A_h + K_* with K_* f = grad h_*.U[f],
where A_h generates a semigroup of norm at most exp(-beta_0 t) and ||K_*|| <= G (since ||U[f]||_2 <= ||f||_2); the
variation-of-constants inequality and Gronwall give ||T_*(t)|| <= exp(-(beta_0 - G) t), and the Neumann argument of
RC-3 (AT-060, AT-123) gives the inverse with norm at most 1/(beta_0 - G) on the same generator and domain. The
semigroup bound is needed, not only the inverse bound; the theory auditor made this step explicit (AT-1483). H3 is (H-a), since
A = -Kmat and so M = -N_q (the numerical auditor's cover contract). H4 is RC-4. H5 holds because W F_* is in every H^s (AT-674,
AT-675), and N(F_*) <= 0.0055546 is certified (V13-5 row 2). The conclusion is T1.2 with beta_0 replaced by
beta_0 - G, and the Hoelder statement is the embedding of NR-1 for alpha <= q - 2 = 1/10. Consequences.
1. The strain component is not used, and the gradient component is not needed at the target 1/4: any certified
   G < 2.00215453 suffices. On the complete annulus 41/87 <= |X|^2 <= 83/173 the CONFIRMED bound is |grad h| <=

   reviewed root gives 71/500 (V13-5 row 3). The target 1/4 matters only for row 7 (beta_0* >= 7/4 in Lemma KB).
2. By the numerical auditor's admission contract a component that passes on every root holds on the whole plane, and a tighter

   target (for example g = 1, which gives beta_0* > 1.00215) or the leaf maximum of the numerical auditor's prepared reduction for

   intersected rh and sh intervals, g_* <= sqrt(B)) applied to the 013 records would supply (H-b). Either is an exact
   rational postprocessing of the saved and replayed leaf intervals with no new field evaluation; it needs its own
   review, and its cost is not measured.
3. So, once the 128 reviewed root replays exist, the matrix component and a weak gradient target are the only

### V13-1. Split bound for the HF1-NEAR kernel constants (continues V12-1; theory_v12 V12-4 (b) 4 (iii))

(g) Split bound for kappa_0, kappa_2q and the top mode-1 piece of kappa_j (UB in ball arithmetic; method and runs
CONFIRMED: AT-1241 and AT-1242 for mode 0, AT-1250 and AT-1251 for mode 1; registered as NR-29 in
THEORY_NEW_RESULTS version 13). Notation of V12-1 and NR-28: w(x) = (1 + 4|x|^2)^(1/2), V^2 a cubic polynomial in
|x|^2 with positive rational coefficients c_n, B_0 to B_3 the Plancherel integrals of NR-28 (i), m the symbol and
K = F^-1 m.
1. Why not a higher degree. With V^2 of degree 3, 4 and 5 in |x|^2 (weights optimized in FLOAT) the Cauchy-Schwarz
   bound of NR-28 (i) over the direct FLOAT value of ||w K||_1 is 1.0879 / 1.0876 / 1.0874 for kappa_0 and
   1.1178 / 1.1169 / 1.1164 for kappa_2q at mu 41.5 (research/kernel_n6/deg5_float.py, runs/deg5_float_mu41_5.out).
   Equality needs V^2 proportional to w/|K|, and K changes sign.
2. Method (research/kernel_n6/split_ub.py). ||w K||_1 = 2 pi int_0^R0 w |K| r dr + int_(|x| > R0) w |K|, and
     int_(|x| > R0) w |K| <= (pi int_(R0^2)^inf (1 + 4u)/V^2(u) du)^(1/2)
                               ((2 pi)^-2 sum_n c_n B_n - 2 pi int_0^R0 V^2 K^2 r dr)^(1/2),
   with the B_n of NR-28 (i). On the disk K(r) = (2 pi)^-1 sum_n (-1)^n (r/2)^(2n) M_n/(n!)^2 with
   M_n = int_0^(2 mu) m k^(2n+1) dk; m >= 0 gives M_n <= (2 mu)^(2n) M_0 for the tails and |K''| <= (2 pi)^-1 M_1
   for the cells (|J0''| <= 1); the M_n are ball integrals with the flat ends of Lemma FE (NR-28 (ii)).

(a) What is bounded. At P-S1 (sigma 1, r0 1/2, w(x) = (1 + 4|x|^2)^(1/2)), with Psi_mu(xi) = P(|xi|/mu - 1),
P(t) = cos((pi/2) S(t)) and S the step of AT-420 (fixed by AT-428), with nu = 1/100 and the free cut psi = Psi_1
(admissible for HF1-NEAR: radial, values in [0, 1], 1 on |xi| <= 1, 0 on |xi| >= 2):
  kappa_0(mu) = ||w F^-1[Psi_mu]||_1,  kappa_2q(mu) = ||w F^-1[Psi_mu <.>^(2q)]||_1,
  kappa_j(nu, mu) = ||w F^-1[omega_j (1 - psi_nu) Psi_mu <.>^q]||_1 (j = 1, 2; equal by rotation),
and kappa_q(mu) = ||w F^-1[Psi_mu <.>^q]||_1 as a diagnostic (not in P_HF). Computed at mu = 41, 41.5, 42, 45, 46,
48, 52, 56, 64 and 80.

(b) Method.
1. Cauchy-Schwarz and Plancherel. For V(x)^2 = c0 + c1 |x|^2 + c2 |x|^4 + c3 |x|^6 with rational c_n > 0,
   ||w K||_1 <= ||w/V||_2 ||V K||_2, with ||w/V||_2^2 = pi int_0^inf (1 + 4u)/(c0 + c1 u + c2 u^2 + c3 u^3) du and
   ||V K||_2^2 = (2 pi)^-2 sum_n c_n B_n, where m is the symbol of K, B_0 = int m^2, B_1 = int |grad m|^2,
   B_2 = int (Lap m)^2 and B_3 = int |grad Lap m|^2 (all symbols here are smooth and compactly supported, or
   <xi>^s times such, so m is in H^3). The c_n are chosen by a FLOAT optimization and then fixed as rationals; the
   bound holds for every choice with c_n > 0.
2. Radial reduction. Mode 0 (m = n(rho)): Lap m = n'' + n'/rho, angular factor 2 pi. Mode 1 (m = cos(theta) n(rho)):
   Lap m = cos(theta) L1 n with L1 n = n'' + n'/rho - n/rho^2, |grad m|^2 integrates to pi (n'^2 + n^2/rho^2), and
   |grad Lap m|^2 to pi ((L1 n)'^2 + (L1 n)^2/rho^2). Each B_n is bounded above by a sum over subintervals I of
   |I| times the upper end of an enclosure of the (nonnegative) integrand on I. The derivatives of n are enclosed by
   arb power series in the centered form (the value at the midpoint plus the radius times the enclosure of the next
   derivative on I). On [0, mu] the mode-0 symbol is <rho>^s and closed forms are used. The grids are float points;
   the support ends lam and 2 lam (which need not be floats) are covered by margins of 2^-40 relative, which is valid
   because the enclosures of the flat ends hold on t <= 1/100 and on t >= 99/100, including t <= 0 and t >= 1.
   ||w/V||_2^2 is bounded by an upper Riemann sum on a geometric grid from 2^-40 to 2^40 with exact float endpoints
   (the integrand is a ratio of an increasing numerator and an increasing denominator, so (1 + 4b)/V^2(a) bounds it on
   [a, b]), plus u0 (1 + 4 u0)/c0 on [0, u0] and (1/(2U^2) + 4/U)/c3 on [U, inf).
3. Telescoping split of kappa_j. With lam_0 = nu, lam_(i+1) >= 2 lam_i and last lam = mu,
   (1 - psi_nu) Psi_mu = sum_i (1 - Psi(./lam_i)) Psi(./lam_(i+1)),
   because Psi(./lam_i) vanishes where Psi(./lam_(i+1)) differs from 1, so each product (1 - Psi(./lam_i))
   Psi(./lam_(i+1)) equals Psi(./lam_(i+1)) - Psi(./lam_i), and the sum telescopes to Psi_mu - psi_nu =
   (1 - psi_nu) Psi_mu (2 nu <= mu). kappa_j is bounded by the sum of the piece bounds (triangle inequality). The
   grid used is lam = 1/100, 1/25, 4/25, 16/25, 64/25, 256/25, mu; the five lower pieces do not depend on mu.
4. Angular refinement (mode 1, exact). F^-1[cos(theta) n(rho)] = i cos(theta) G_1(r) with a real radial G_1. Then
   ||w K||_1 = 4 int_0^inf |G_1| w r dr and ||V K||_2^2 = pi int_0^inf V^2 G_1^2 r dr, and Cauchy-Schwarz in r alone
   gives ||w K||_1 <= 4 (W/(2 pi))^(1/2) (||V K||_2^2/pi)^(1/2) = (2 sqrt 2/pi) ||w/V||_2 ||V K||_2, with
   W = ||w/V||_2^2. So every mode-1 piece bound of item 1 times 2 sqrt(2)/pi = 0.9003 is again an upper bound. The
   factor is applied in arb in research/kernel_n6/n6_price.py.
5. Lemma FE (flat ends of the step). Let 0 < delta <= 1/100 and phi = exp(-1/(1 - 3 delta/2)). For 0 < t <= delta
   and |z - t| <= t/2:
   - the disk |z - t| <= t/2 is mapped by 1/z onto the disk with diameter [2/(3t), 2/t], so Re(1/z) >= 2/(3t) and
     |exp(-1/z)| <= exp(-2/(3t));
   - |z| <= 3 delta/2, so |1 - z| >= 1 - 3 delta/2, Re(1/(1 - z)) <= 1/(1 - 3 delta/2) and |exp(-1/(1 - z))| >= phi;
   - S(z) = exp(-1/z)/(exp(-1/z) + exp(-1/(1 - z))) is analytic on the disk, and since exp(-2/(3 delta)) < phi/2,
     |S(z)| <= 2 exp(-2/(3t))/phi =: s(t);
   - with w = (pi/2) S(z), |P(z) - 1| = |cos w - 1| <= (|w|^2/2) cosh|w|; near t = 1, P(1 - tau) = sin((pi/2) S(tau))
     (S(1 - tau) = 1 - S(tau)) and |sin w| <= |w| cosh|w|;
   - Cauchy's estimate on the circle of radius t/2: |P^(k)(t)| <= k! (2/t)^k sup|P - 1| for k >= 1, and the same with
     sup|P| at 1 - t.
   The bounds are increasing in t on (0, 2/(3k)] (t^-k exp(-2/(3t)) increases there), so their values at t = delta
   bound them on (0, delta]; at delta = 1/100 this holds for k <= 66 (the code uses k <= 5 and asserts
   delta <= 2/(3 kmax)). For t <= 0, P = 1, and for t >= 1, P = 0. This gives the enclosures of P and its first four
   derivatives on t <= 1/100 and t >= 99/100, where the arb series of S lose all accuracy.

kappa_j as (4/pi)/nu (the weighted mass of a Riesz kernel x_j/(2 pi |x|^3) cut sharply at |x| = 1/nu). With the
compact Gevrey-type cut psi = Psi_1 the actual part is about (2/nu) C_low, with
C_low = int |y| |F^-1[omega_1 (1 - psi)](y)| dy = 8.94 (FLOAT; proxy: the piece (psi(./16) - psi) omega_1,
research/kernel_n6/runs/kdirect_mu64.out), so 1788 at nu 0.01 against the model 127, a factor 14. The reason is that
the transform of the step decays only like exp(-c |y|^(1/2)), so the kernel of omega_1 (1 - psi) has a heavy tail at
|y| from 1 to about 100. The section 4 sentence "its weighted mass is about (4/pi)/nu + O(log mu)" is withdrawn for
compactly supported psi of this class (on this FLOAT evidence; no bound shows that the model is low, AT-1096). The
direct FLOAT sum of the three nu-scale pieces at nu 0.01 is 2542.

Notation of V11-1. h_* = -Delta phi with phi the exact 013 correction, rho_* = rho_bar + h_*, u_* = u_bar + U[h_*],
F_* = F + L h_* + U[h_*].grad h_*. P-S1: q = 21/10, sigma = 1, r0 = 1/2, W(X) = (1 + 4|X|^2)^(1/2), N(G) = \|\|J^q(W
G)\|\|_2 with J = (1 - Delta)^(1/2). The ball is the full real S1 ball B(Rbar, Mbar) = {k real, even in x, odd in y:
\|\|k\|\|_2 <= Rbar, N(k) <= Mbar}, with no ell restriction (chain item 7).

(a) Statement (conditional; RC theorem T2.7, AT-123, with Lemma KB, AT-598, and the H4 convention of AT-114). Assume:
1. RC-1 to RC-10 for h_* (the structural ones are supplied by the exact-potential class, AT-674, AT-675; the
   quantitative ones are chain items 2 and 3);
2. certified \|\|F_*\|\|_2 <= f and N(F_*) <= n, a certified cover with N_q* <= -beta_* I on R^2, beta_* >= 3/5,
   g_* <= 1/4 and s_* <= c - A/q, where A is a certified far upper of the far route used (V11-3, V11-4);
3. a certified near upper (HF1-NEAR, V11-5) and the far upper A, combined in the frozen estimate with the constants
   of the H4 convention;

   M <= Mbar, with loss < 0.152070 (Lemma KB on that rectangle).
Then there is a stationary solution h = h_* + k of the profile problem with k in B(Rbar, M): k is real and S1,
\|\|k\|\|_2 <= Rbar and W k is in H^(21/10)(R^2) with \|\|J^(21/10)(W k)\|\|_2 <= M <= 1/2. The full linearization L_* +
U[k].grad has the full L^2 inverse of T2.7 with rate beta_0* and the weighted estimate
    (betaK_* - eps) N(z) <= N(G) + (1 + delta0) N(k) \|\|grad z\|\|_inf + sqrt((betaK_* - eps) Cbar) \|\|z\|\|_2.

(b) Regularity of the solution (Sobolev route; this is what the chain gives without further premises).
- k: H^(21/10)(R^2) embeds in C^(1,1/10)(R^2), so W k is in C^(1,1/10) with \|\|W k\|\|_(C^(1,1/10)) <= C_S(21/10, 1/10)
  M. Then <X> k is in C^(1,1/10) with the multiplier norm of <X>/W (finite; a pointwise bound of <X>/W is not this
  multiplier norm, AT-097).
- h_*: phi is in the exact-potential class, so h_* is C^infinity with all-order decay (AT-674, AT-675; gamma_h = 6 -
  4/c), and W h_* is in every H^s.
- Hence h = h_* + k and the profile rho = rho_bar + h have W(h - h_*) in H^(21/10) and <X> h in C^(1,1/10): the
  solution has the endpoint regularity C^(1,1/10) with weight <X>^1.
This is the full regularity that the P-S1 chain provides. It is not more: alpha = q - 2 = 1/10 is the Sobolev endpoint
at q = 21/10.

(c) Structural certificate of the top eigenvalue (coordinator route (i)).
- Sign-definite pieces of T_a. Q_a depends on a only modulo constants (sum_j R_j^* R_j = I), so a one-signed
  decomposition of a carries no information (the second numerics agent v02 withdrew the sign-definiteness sentence). In the spatial form
  T_a = sum_j R_j^* a R_j - a, the pieces with a_+ and a_- have natural bounds whose sum is sup a_+ - inf a, an
  oscillation-type value (FLOAT 0.771 > 0.629). The AT-874 diagonal-plus-low-rank criterion, written with
  W = (sqrt(a_+) R_j)_j, gives the test \|\|W (U + M_a)^(-1) W^*\|\| <= 1, whose plain bound returns the same value.
  Scope (AT-915, AT-916): the test is sufficient when U + M_a is uniformly positive and then gives Q_a <= U only, so
  the full B_a still needs its C_aw (J-commutator) estimate; it is not necessary once the negative part -V^*V is
  dropped (AT-916 REFUTED the equivalence with an exact 2 x 2 example), and the exact positive-denominator test uses
  U + M_a + V^*V. No linear-size structure below the oscillation is known for this operator.
- Semiclassical structure. On the FLOAT spectra the band top at this split is a high-frequency packet where SC is
  attained (the second numerics agent; band values 0.385, 0.426, 0.445 at 8, 16, 32 pi rise toward SC 0.4605). A positive quantization
  of the principal symbol (1/2)[Delta a + (q^2 - 1) d_omega^2 a], whose supremum is SC, with an explicit remainder,
  is what Lemma HSB already does with a band for the low frequencies and the Schur cost as remainder. A sharper
  remainder than S_h^B would let K' drop: at 2 pi the band order is 1.6e4 at L 128, but S_h^B = 0.1834 leaves an SC
  margin of 0.0084. What it must prove: an off-band remainder bound below S_h^B with constants from certified D^3 a
  and D^4 a bounds of the far piece. Not written; I do not expect it before the stop.
- Residual plus complement upper (AT-875, AT-914, CONFIRMED). The coordinator's arithmetic is correct: with lambda,
  sigma <= T, the bound U <= T holds iff \|\|r\|\|^2 <= (T - lambda)(T - sigma). The saved residuals (the second numerics agent 12:14Z:
  8.7e-10 at 8 pi, L 128) are negligible: the correction U - max(lambda, sigma) is at most \|\|r\|\| always and at
  most \|\|r\|\|^2/d when the gap d = \|lambda - sigma\| is positive (AT-962 REFUTED a uniform O(\|\|r\|\|^2) form),
  so everything rests on the complement upper sigma. A nonzero residual forces both diagonal bounds strictly below
  T, and a failed test does not show that the operator exceeds T (AT-914). All known uppers are whole-band bounds
  above the room (AT-882, AT-886), and removing a finite trial space does not lower them; the top is a cluster (62
  to 98 matvecs for 1e-7 at 16 pi), so a short trial space leaves near-top states in the complement. A cheaper sigma
  needs T <= sigma + (finite rank) + small, which is a localization lemma of the kind in (b) 2. Block form with the
  referee's annulus bound: on kappa <= \|xi\| <= K' the Q part is at most (1/2)(1 + kappa^(-2)) M2(a_f), and with
  the OMF term (q^2/2) M2[w_new](a_f) as the C_aw charge the complement charge is at least (1/2)(M2 + (q^2/2)
  M2[w_new]) = (1/2)(OMF - osc) = (1/2)(3.81 - 0.771) = 1.52 for every kappa (FLOAT), above the budget 0.629. A
  sharper C_aw bound on the annulus would be needed. At K' = 4 pi the same holds with budget 0.5805.

(d) Regularity and the meaning of M4. The numerical auditor 12:29Z (numerical_audit/research/source013_near_hypotheses/PROOF.md) proves that
a_n = (1 - cut) atil for erflog 8, rho 1, with the cut extended by zero at the origin, is a real Schwartz function
on R^2 under the finite exact atom conditions it checks (the canonical 007 atom classes and the 013 correction
atoms; source identity from the accepted conversion proofs). Review (the first theory agent): the argument is correct. The atoms are
smooth with polynomially growing derivatives, since every power of (a + s) and (1 + s) has a + s > 0; every
derivative of the cut is a finite sum of r^(-j) P(log(r/R)) exp(-log(r/R)^2/L^2) and vanishes faster than every
power at 0 and, for 1 - cut, at infinity; Leibniz then gives all Schwartz seminorms; and (1 + \|xi\|^2)^4
\|a_n^\| <= \|\|(1 - Delta)^4 a_n\|\|_1 gives a_n^ in L^1 and M4 finite in dimension 2. So the qualitative
hypotheses of HF1-NEAR (real, C^2 with bounded Hessian, a_n^ in L^1, M4, A, A_+, L_+ finite) hold for the 013 near
piece, conditional on the imported exact-source identities (the theory auditor AT-928 CONFIRMED, with evenness in both
coordinates by reflection parity; AT-929 CONFIRMED the atom hypotheses for all 1922 base terms and 12273 correction
atoms; AT-931 OPEN for every numerical constant). This is N1 below. It gives finiteness only, no constant.
Consequence for M4 (reading, not a proof): the M4 that a certificate needs is that of the exact Schwartz a_n. The
sampled value 5017.9 is a grid quantity. The second numerics agent 11:34Z item 2 finds it dominated by an interpolation floor (2661 at h
0.03, 1900 to 2000 for a smooth evaluation). A C^2 piecewise cubic interpolant whose third derivative jumps across
circles has \|a^\| of order \|zeta\|^(-9/2), so its continuum M4 (weight \|zeta\|^4 in two dimensions) diverges;
refining a spline does not converge to the exact M4. The certified route is NR-25 (AT-890 to AT-892) from interval
bounds of \|\|D^k a_n\|\|_2, k = 4, ..., 6, computed from the closed-form atoms.

### V10-1. The far upper on rho in [1, 2]: Lemma HS, Corollary HS-R, Lemma HSB and the FLOAT table

This answers coordinator 08:10Z item 3(b), first part, and 09:35Z item 3(b).
Setting: the far form B_a(g) = Q_a(g) + C_aw[a](g) of the complete 009 far part a = a_f, and v = J^-1 g. A far
constant A in B_a(g) <= A ||J^-1 g||^2 fits under the gain G = q(c - S) of Proposition FG exactly when S >= 0 and
A <= q(c - S), i.e. when a certified strain upper s_* satisfies s_* <= c - A/q. Gbar = q(c - 3/2) = 0.6517 and
q = 2.1 are the two reference gains (FLOAT decimals of exact expressions).

(a) Statements and status.
- Lemma HS (the first theory agent; research/far_hh/HS_DERIVATION.md). For real bounded a with int |a^| (1 + |zeta|^2) d zeta finite,
  multipliers 0 <= phi, theta <= 1, a positive weight h and a finite Schur cost S_h:
  B_a(g) <= SC(a) ||Phi v||^2 + osc(a) ||Theta v||^2 + S_h ||v||^2, and in the partition case
  (phi^2 + theta^2 <= 1) B_a(g) <= [max(SC(a), osc(a)) + S_h] ||v||^2. SC(a) is the Hessian combination
  sup_x max(0, (1/2)[(q^2 - 1) lambda_max Hess a + tr Hess a]), the floor of Lemma SC-LB. PROVED in the scope of
  AT-664. AT-666 corrections: the rows need not be Lipschitz in xi under these hypotheses alone, and M2 alone does not
  make S_h finite; a certificate must prove the row regularity it uses.
- Corollary HS-R (the first theory agent, row-wise form). With the Schur row rho_h(xi) = (2 pi)^-2 int (1/2) |a^(xi - eta)| |r(xi, eta)|
  h(eta)/h(xi) d eta, B_a(g) <= ess sup_xi [SC(a) phi(|xi|)^2 + osc(a) theta(|xi|)^2 + rho_h(xi)] ||v||^2. It is never
  larger than the partition form. PROVED conditionally (AT-706: under the explicit finite continuum hypotheses and the
  original multiplier conditions).
- Lemma HSB (the second theory agent, T2 notes 09:37Z item 5). With theta = cos alpha, phi = sin alpha and
  alpha = (pi/2) clip((|xi| - K)/(K' - K)), B_a(g) <= [max(SC(a), A_low(K')) + S_h^B] ||v||^2, where A_low(K') is the
  best constant of B_a on g with Fourier support in |xi| <= K'. CONFIRMED conditionally (AT-695: a^ in L^1, finite
  M2, a certified S_h^B and the continuum A_low(K')). The remainder vanishes on the low-low square (AT-696,
  CONFIRMED). Its row-wise form (the first theory agent, note 37 item 4(b)) is PROVED conditionally with HS-R (AT-706).
- Lemma HS, general form (the first theory agent; answers the second theory agent's proposal of 09:49Z and coordinator 10:05Z item 4(d) to state HS
  with HSB as a corollary). PROVED conditionally: AT-756 CONFIRMED cases (O) and (B), the row-wise form and the
  partition consequence under the finite continuum hypotheses (a real and bounded, M0 + M2 = int (1 + |zeta|^2) |a^|
  finite, measurable radial 0 <= phi, theta <= 1, a positive measurable weight h and a finite S_h^L; in case (B) the
  continuum A_low(K') on the same real test space, with radial cutoffs preserving any parity space). Keep the
  setting of HS_DERIVATION.md section 2 and put Ktil(xi, eta) = <xi><eta> K(xi, eta) (the kernel of B_a in v = J^-1 g,
  Lemma KER') and P(xi, eta) = |zeta|^2 (w.w') + (q^2 - 1)(zeta.w)(zeta.w'). Choose a low-band kernel L and a constant
  Lambda in one of two ways:
  (O) L = |w - w'|^2 and Lambda = osc(a) (Lemma OSC, AT-451);
  (B) theta(t) = 0 for t > K', L = Ktil and Lambda = A_low(K') (the best constant of B_a on tests with Fourier support
      in |xi| <= K').
  With r_L = Ktil - phi(|xi|) phi(|eta|) P - theta(|xi|) theta(|eta|) L and S_h^L the weighted Schur cost of
  -(1/2) a^ r_L, B_a(g) <= SC(a) ||Phi v||^2 + Lambda ||Theta v||^2 + S_h^L ||v||^2. Proof: Steps 1, 2 and 4 of HS
  unchanged. Step 3 in case (O) is the HS step. In case (B) the theta-term is S[-(1/2) a^ theta theta' Ktil](v) =
  B_a(J Theta v); J Theta v has Fourier support in |xi| <= K' and J^-1 (J Theta v) = Theta v, so the term is at most
  A_low(K') ||Theta v||^2 by the definition of A_low(K'). Case (O) is Lemma HS (r_L = r). Case (B) with
  theta = cos alpha and phi = sin alpha is Lemma HSB (phi^2 + theta^2 = 1; on |xi|, |eta| <= K one has phi = 0 and
  theta = 1, so r_L = 0 on the low-low block |xi|, |eta| <= K, AT-696; it does not vanish on the whole row
  |xi| <= K, AT-758). The row-wise form of HS-R holds in both cases with r_L in the row. A third instance is case (O)
  with a band-supported theta: L = |w - w'|^2, theta = 0 for t > K', and Lambda the band-limited L^2 constant of Q_a
  alone (the low term of case (O) is Q_a(Theta v)), which is at most osc(b) for every real bounded b with b^ = a^ on
  |zeta| <= 2K' (AT-707). (The draft form
  L = theta theta' |w - w'|^2 inserted the cutoff twice and represents Q_a(Theta^2 v), AT-760.) Certificate inputs for
  any instance: item (d) below.

### V10-2. Proposition HF1-NEAR: the HF-1 near price with the combined form (research/hf1_near/HF1_NEAR.md)

(a) Statement. Let a = a_n be the near part, with (N1) the AT-428 hypotheses (a in C^2 with bounded Hessian, a^ in
L^1, M4(a) finite), (N2) sup(|a| W^2), sup(a_+ W^2) and ||a_+||_1 finite, and (N3) the kernel constants
kappa_s^Psi(mu) = ||w_sigma F^-1[Psi_mu <.>^s]||_1 (s = 0, 2q) and
kappa_j^Psi(nu, mu) = ||w_sigma F^-1[omega_j (1 - psi_nu) Psi_mu <.>^q]||_1 (j = 1, 2) finite, with 0 < 2 nu <= mu,
mu >= 1. Then for every t in (0, 1) and every h with g = J^q W h in L^2,
  (TII + C_aw)[a](g) <= e_HF ||g||^2 + P_HF ||h||^2,
  e_HF = (1 + q^2) Lambda_+(a)/(2 mu^2) + (pi^2 (1 + c_aw/2) + C_D/2) M4(a)/mu^4 + 2^q T_q(a; mu/2)
         + t^-1 pi^-1 ||a_+||_1 nu^2,
  P_HF = 2^sigma [ sup(|a| W^2) kappa_0^Psi(mu) kappa_2q^Psi(mu)
                 + (1 - t)^-1 sup(a_+ W^2) sum_j kappa_j^Psi(nu, mu)^2 ].
Status: PROVED conditionally (AT-691: both inequalities hold under N1 to N3 with mu >= 1, 2 nu <= mu, h in L2 and
the four finite weighted kernel norms). The floor of Remark 2 (P_HF >= 2^sigma c (1 + mu^2)^q and
mu^2 >= 4 (1 + q^2)(2c - 1)/(cap - b0)) is CONFIRMED within this construction (AT-692); it is not a lower bound for
C^opt and excludes no other construction. The three-piece split of the Riesz multiplier is an algebraic identity
(AT-693, CONFIRMED); a complete numerical price is OPEN (AT-693, AT-694). Tail variant: e_HF holds with
2^q T_q(a; mu/2) replaced by (4/3)^q T_q(a; 3 mu/4) + (8/mu)^q T_q(a; mu/2) and P_HF unchanged (AT-757, CONFIRMED
under the same hypotheses; V10-4 (b)). Both tails are of the actual near coefficient a_n; the price tables of V10-4
use a weight-part proxy, which neither audit covers.

(b) What it changes. The combined form sum_j <a R_j f, R_j f> - Re <a J^-q f, J^q f> has no <a f, f> term, so the
near price loses the term T_- = 2^sigma sup((a_n)_- W^2) kappa_q^2 of a separate treatment of TII and C_aw
(Proposition TII-0 of the second theory agent and its P_A, P_B). The Riesz part is priced by the band split at nu: Cauchy-Schwarz below
nu (an e-term, not a price), Peetre and Young above.

(c) What a certificate needs: uppers for Lambda_+(a_n) (the floor 8 (2c - 1) of AT-575 is a lower), M4(a_n),
T_q(a_n; mu/2), sup(|a_n| W^2), sup((a_n)_+ W^2) and ||(a_n)_+||_1, and certified uppers of the four kernel constants
(one-dimensional Hankel integrals of the mode-0 and mode-1 symbols with explicit tails).

### V10-4. The far/near split priced with HF1-NEAR (coordinator 10:05Z item 4(d); the second theory agent 09:46Z item 4)

(a) The two conditions. A split (cut, rho) of the background coefficient into a near part a_n and a far part a_f
passes the H4 step when both hold, and they are independent apart from the shared split:
- Far: a certified far constant A_far with A_far <= G = q(c - S), S a certified strain upper (the sufficient (FG1)
  rule, AT-624). G = 1.5 needs S <= 1.0960, G = 2 needs S <= 0.85793 (the numerical auditor's target), Gbar = 0.6517 needs S <= 3/2.
  The far values are those of V10-1.
- Near: P_HF <= D(b0) for some rate b0, where mu solves e_HF = cap - b0 (V10-2) and D is the V10-3 budget. The gain G
  does not enter the near test. So "the log 8, rho 1 split at G = 1.5" passes the far test with the HSB value 1.368
  (S <= 1.158 needed; G = 1.5 asks S <= 1.0960, which is stronger), and "the erflog 16, rho 1 split at G = 2" passes it
  with HS-R 0.794 (S <= 1.432 needed); in both cases the near test is the same table row whatever G is.

(b) Inputs of the price (research/hf1_near/hf1_price.py, runs/hf1_price.out, 10:20Z). The second theory agent's far_scan rows of the
complete 009 coefficient (b14s, N 2048, K 8): sup((a_n)_- W^2), sup((a_n)_+ W^2), ||(a_n)_+||_1, Lambda_+(a_n) with
the floor 8 (2c - 1) = 20.965 (AT-575) in its place where larger, M4(a_n) (rows with near spacing above 0.0305,

kappa_0, kappa_2q from the second theory agent's kappa_ims_tab.out; kappa_j = r_j kappa_q + (4/pi)/nu with r_j = kappa_j^(b)/kappa_q
from runs/kappa_j_tab.out (0.651 at mu 10 to 0.659 at mu 150, interpolated in log mu). Tail A is the IMS tail

Hypotheses for the erflog cut (the second theory agent 10:48Z item 2 asks). The erflog cut is not compactly supported: at lam 8,
chi(rho) = 0.006 and chi(8 rho) = 0.994, so a_f does not vanish on r < rho and a_n does not vanish on r > 8 rho.
Neither lemma needs compact support. Proposition HF1-NEAR (AT-691, AT-757) asks of the near coefficient: a real C^2
function with bounded Hessian, a^ in L^1, finite M4, finite A = sup(|a_n| W^2), A_+ = sup((a_n)_+ W^2) and
L_+ = ||(a_n)_+||_1, and the four weighted kernel norms. Lemma HS (AT-756) asks of the far coefficient: real and
bounded with M0 + M2 finite. The split a = a_n + a_f is exact for chi + (1 - chi) = 1. For the erflog cut, 1 - chi
decays like exp(-C log^2 r), faster than every power of r, so A, A_+ and L_+ are finite whenever a is bounded; this
is a reading, not a checked statement for the actual fields. What the non-compact support changes is the
certificate: the sampled A, A_+, L_+ and M4 are taken on the computational window, and the part of a_n outside that
window must be bounded explicitly. The same applies to the erflog 16 rows of (c), (c2) and (d).

### V10-5. Audit outcomes AT-640 to AT-807 and the corrections they require

(a) Corrections to theory_v09 and to notes 36 and 37. Each item names the audit entry; theory_v09 is not edited, and
the carried-over sections below are read with these corrections.
1. AT-645 (REFUTED, the literal radius). V9-5, "Fit to the HF-Q witnesses": the auxiliary radii of the budget
   witnesses are not all below 0.497. The exact largest value is 0.49729448368455, which is below 0.498. The trial
   radii satisfy M <= 0.495 < 1/2 (AT-633), so Mbar = 1/2 still contains every auxiliary radius and the conclusion of
   V9-5 (RC-10 needs no certificate of its own at b0 >= 0.150314) is unchanged. Corrected sentence: "their auxiliary
   radii are below 0.498".
2. AT-646 (REFUTED as a sufficient rule). The statement in theory_v09 (response to coordinator 06:25Z, and T6.3) that
   the cell rule of Proposition TII0-RHO "needs only point values of the coefficient" is wrong for the stronger form.
   The positive-part switch of that form uses an integral premise, and smooth bumps with fixed point values and
   arbitrarily small integrals show that point values cannot supply it. The stronger cell bound needs a certified
   lower of the integral over a set of positive area (or equivalent quantitative information). The weaker variant
   with the switch off needs point values only. Proposition TII0-RHO (AT-549) keeps its scope with this premise named.
   Whether the exclusion figures of V9-4 hold with the weaker variant is not rechecked here (OPEN); a certificate of
   the stronger form needs point lowers plus an integral lower. Under coordinator 07:37Z item 3(a) no further TII-0
   work is done.
3. AT-650 (REFUTED as a general bound). Note 36 stated that the exact-kernel Schur approach gains at most about 1.23
   over TII-1 plus CAW-F, so that a factor 2.5 would need signs. That ceiling holds only for the separately qualified
   principal-symbol comparison. For a smooth radial Fourier-annulus coefficient at q = 2.1 and nu = 100 an
   absolute-kernel improvement above 3.71515 exists. The far tables of V10-1 are consistent with this: at log 8, rho 1
   the row-wise HSB value 1.368 is 14 times below A_a = 19.36 (FLOAT).
4. Note 37 item 3 (the first theory agent erratum, found in this version). The log 16, rho 1 strain level from HS-R is 1.256 (from
   1.165), not 1.250, and the sentence "s_* <= 3/2 makes none of the computed rows fit" is wrong (V10-1 (c)).
5. AT-726, AT-727. 20 CE witnesses of budget_013a at b0 0.7103 had M > 1/2 (maximum 0.506), outside the domain of
   Lemma KB. Repaired witnesses with M = 1/2 keep all 20 printed D lowers; 14 Z lowers need the revised decimals. The
   D tables of V10-3 and V10-4 use budget_013c, budget_013d and budget_013e, where M is clamped to M <= 1/2 (printed as
   "M 0.5 clamped").
6. AT-737 (REFUTED). The one-epsilon summation estimate "2.2e-16 times the absolute term sum" is false for sequential
   accumulation (four inputs 1, u, u, u with u = 2^-53 return 1). No theory statement of theory_v01 to theory_v09
   uses it. Any FLOAT accuracy statement that does should use the gamma_(M-1) bound of AT-738 (CONFIRMED under its

- The second theory agent 10:57Z item 3 gives a transfer route for the far constants, and its structure is right. The far form B_a is
  linear in a. So for the windowed difference d_f of the two far pieces, the OMF baseline (AT-664 to AT-667) applied
  to d_f and to -d_f gives |B_(d_f)(g)| <= OMF(d_f) ||J^-1 g||_2^2. Hence a far upper A of the 009 piece gives
  A + OMF(d_f) for the 013 piece at the same split and window, and SC(a_f(013)) <= SC(a_f(009)) + SC(d_f), because
  SC is subadditive. The route bounds the whole difference form and does not pass through the Schur cost of the
  difference, which a sup norm and a second moment do not control (AT-759). Its hypotheses are those of the OMF
  baseline for d_f (real, bounded, finite osc, M2 and M2[w_new]). The FLOAT envelope OMF(d_f) is about 8.5e-4 at
  six splits (largest printed value 8.509e-4, not a directed upper), which moves the strain level by about 4.1e-4.
  The second theory agent's notes that the sampled difference has a high-frequency floor at the node scale, so these values are envelopes.
  A certificate needs certified uppers of the three norms of the true correction difference, preferably from the exact
  phi files. The transfer applies to the two windowed forms with the same cut, radius and window; the unwindowed
  coefficients need the true unwindowed difference or certified window-removal bounds. The theory auditor's draft audit
  (research/source013_far_transfer) states this conditional theorem with the same hypotheses; no verdict was published
  at this writing.

### V10-7. Most sensitive constants and candidate changes that would help (P-S1, from V10-1 to V10-4; HEURISTIC)

These items replace V9-7 and V9-8 where they differ. The constants are ranked by their effect on the H4 test at the
013 inputs, near side and far side together. Every number is FLOAT or a stipulated input.

(a) Most sensitive constants.
1. The forcing upper f (certified ||F_*||_2 <= f). D scales close to f^-2 (Z = D R^2 is constant to 1 percent across f,
   V10-3 (d)): D rises by a factor 1.50 to 1.51 from f 1e-6 to 8.2e-7 and by 1.58 to 8e-7. For 013 the float-grid value
   is 1.0063e-6 and the noise-free FLOAT values are 7.90e-7 (the second numerics agent) and 7.96e-7 (the first numerics agent), so the precision of the
   certified evaluation alone moves D by a factor of about 1.6. The lowers act on the necessary side: U grows roughly
   like l^-2, while the G1 levels move by less than 0.3 percent between l 7.6e-7 and 7.9e-7 (V10-3 (c)).
2. The far split (cut and rho). It sets the floor SC(a_f) of every far upper (Lemma SC-LB) and the near price. At
   rho 1 the floor is 0.968 for log 8, 0.419 to 0.4275 for log 16 and 0.4598 for erflog 8 (V10-1 (b)), and the strain
   level c - A_far/q of the best row is 1.158, 1.590 and 1.583. Whether the cover target 3/2 suffices depends only on
   this choice (V10-6 (c)).
3. M4(a_n). The near price grows by a factor 1.5 to 1.9 per doubling of M4 (V10-4 (e)): mu grows like M4^(1/4) where
   the M4 term dominates e_HF, and the kernel constants like mu^(2q). A certified M4 within a factor 2 of the sampled
   value keeps the log 16 and erflog 16 rows below D at b0 0.55 and 0.60 (f 1e-6, n 0.0055); a factor 4 fails at b0
   0.60 and passes only at b0 0.55 (AT-777). At
   erflog 8, rho 1 the price is about 0.55 times that of log 16, rho 1 (the second theory agent 10:48Z), so it tolerates about one
   further doubling.
4. A_low(K') against SC(a_f). In every computed HSB row the box value lies below SC, so the lead is SC and the
   certificate needs A_low(K') <= SC(a_f) (V10-1 (d) 2). The FLOAT margins: erflog 8, rho 1: 0.3848 against 0.4598
   (16 percent); erflog 8, rho 0.9: 0.4735 against 0.5778 (18 percent); log 16, rho 1.5: continuum 0.170 to 0.175
   against 0.1873 (9 percent, the second numerics agent 10:38Z, after a 6 percent box effect). If a certified A_low lies above SC, it
   replaces SC as the lead and the far value rises by the difference.
5. The Schur cost S_h^B. It is the excess of HSB over its lead: 0.0227, 0.0369, 0.0479 and 0.0817 at erflog 8, rho 1,
   0.9, 0.85 and 0.75; 0.0345 at log 16, rho 1; 0.416 at log 8, rho 1. A certified upper needs the weighted remainder
   integral itself; a sup norm and a second moment of a coefficient difference do not bound its change (AT-759).
6. The strain s_*. The far test asks s_* <= c - A_far/q. The sampled s_* equals the origin value c - 1 = 0.8103
   (FLOAT, AT-602), far below every level in V10-1 (b), so the sensitivity lies in the target the certified cover
   must reach: 3/2 for the rows under Gbar and 1.096 for the rows between Gbar and 1.5 (V10-6 (c)). At the 009
   budgets it is 1.160 or below (erflog 8, rho 0.6, V10-6 (d)).
7. b0. D grows with b0 (at f 1e-6, n 0.0055: 7.71e10 at b0 0.55 to 1.74e11 at 0.7103), while the near price is
   smallest at b0 0.55 to 0.60 and exceeds D by factors 2 to 40 at b0 0.70, where cap - b0 = 0.0103 leaves little
   room for e_HF (V10-4 (d)). The near test is therefore best run at b0 0.55 to 0.60.
8. beta_0* and N_(21/10). D at beta_0* 93/50 is about 1.14 times D at 7/4 (f 8e-7, b0 0.6, N 0.0161). D at N 0.0055 is
   about 1.15 times D at N 0.0161 (f 1e-6, b0 0.6). The FLOAT N_(21/10) of 013 is 0.005446 (the second numerics agent 09:38Z); whether

### V9-1. G1 necessary levels as functions of a certified source lower l (coordinator 06:06Z item 3(e))

Statement. Consider an HF-Q test (CE input or original input) at P-S1 or P-S2 at rate b0. Suppose ||F_*||_2 >= l is
certified, and let 0 < beta0 <= c + 1 be arbitrary. Then a passing test needs N(F_*) below the strict upper in the
table. Status: CONFIRMED conditionally for every printed cell (AT-521; l stipulated; full necessary-test hypotheses).
Source: research/qwg/v02/hfq_ps1/necr_b14s/levels_vs_l.py and levels_vs_l.out.

Use rules:
- Rounding (AT-519, CONFIRMED). The level is nonincreasing in l and nondecreasing in b0. Round a certified lower down
  to a table row, and round the rate up to a column.
- Interpolation (AT-520, CONFIRMED). The envelope is jointly convex in (b0, l). A chord between two strict uppers of
  the same row or the same column is a valid upper at interior points, and so is bilinear interpolation from four
  corners. No extrapolation outside 1e-6 <= l <= 1e-5.
- Size of the l-dependence (AT-522). Between l = 1e-6 and 1e-5 the columns with b0 >= 0.60 drop by about 4.36 to 4.46
  percent (P-S1) and 3.94 to 3.99 percent (P-S2) (rounded descriptions).
- Low rates. The low-rate column at l = 2.76e-6 is AT-501 (T2.2).
- Inserting the numerical auditor's lower. When the numerical auditor certifies ||F_*||_2 >= l*, take the largest row l <= l*, or the chord between
  the two neighbouring rows.

The column b0 = 0.2598005590205 is an upward rounding of the AT-503 rate bound 0.25980055902044.

### V9-3. H4 at P-S1 at the exact stipulated inputs: permitted ||F_*||_2 and the strong-residual allowance

All D values are sufficient budgets for the CE input at P-S1: if C^opt(b0) <= D and the other retained hypotheses hold,
the test passes. They are lower decimals from explicit witnesses. Every U value is a necessary budget: a pass needs
C^opt(b0) < U (Corollary BUD-NEC). U holds at every beta0 <= c + 1 unless a beta0 is named. D and U bracket the supremum
of the admissible scalar budgets, not C^opt(b0) itself (AT-396, AT-417). Inputs are stipulated (AT-567: the tables do
not certify the actual 009 test).

(a) The rate beta_0* that the certificate chain can supply. By RC-3 the always-permitted rate is
beta_0* = beta_0 - g_*, with the certified beta_0 > 2.00215453 (AN-010) and g_* = ||grad h_*||_inf (AT-060, AT-123).
- The value 209/100 used in theory_v08 lies above 2.00215453. It is therefore not available by this rule at any
  center; it would need a separate certificate (AT-123 item 3).
- The rate 187/100 needs g_* <= 0.13215453. The sampled FLOAT g_* is 0.1356 to 0.1378 at every center (V9-2), so
  187/100 is not supported. Its rows are kept for orientation only.

Lemma KB (new; research/recenter_g2/KBALL.md; PROVED: CONFIRMED by the theory auditor in AT-598, evaluation AT-599).
- Setting. P-S1, Kbar = {k real S1: ||k||_2 <= Rb, N(k) <= Mb}.
- Bounds. For all A, B > 8q, sup over k in Kbar and X of lambda_max Sym DU[k](X) <= S(A) = Rb A^2/(8 sqrt(2
      pi)) + mu(A) Mb (I3(A)/(32 pi))^(1/2), sup over k in Kbar and X of |U[k](X)| <= V(B) = Rb B (3/(32
      pi))^(1/2) + mu(B) Mb (3 I1(B)/(16 pi))^(1/2).
  Here I3(A) = int_A^infinity r^3 (1 + r^2)^(-q) dr and I1(B) = int_B^infinity r (1 + r^2)^(-q) dr.
  The factor mu(A) = 1/(1 - 4q/A) + e^(-A/4)(U^3 + 6U^2 + 24U + 48) with U = 1 + A/2 bounds the weight transfer
  through the positive transform of 1/W.
- Consequence. betaK_* >= beta* - q S(A) - (sigma/(2 r0)) V(B).
- Proof. The difference of the RC-10 and RC-5 matrices is q Sym DU[k] - (U[k].grad log W) I. Low frequencies are bounded
  through ||k||_2 and high frequencies through N(k).
- Evaluation (Arb, upward rounding; kball_margin3.out). The loss is below 0.150314 at Rb = 2.8476e-6/(7/4) and
  Mb = 1/2. The external referee referee places the optimum in (0.15031319457946938, 0.15031319457946940). The loss is below
  0.149691 at beta_0* = 187/100 (orientation, V9-3 (a)), below 0.150833 at a size of 3e-6 and below 0.164140 at 1e-5
  (Mb 1/2, beta_0* 7/4).
- Fit to the HF-Q witnesses. The audited trial radii satisfy M <= 0.495 < 1/2 (AT-633), and their auxiliary radii
  (the scalar Kbar of the budget scripts, not the set above) are below 0.497, so Mbar = 1/2 contains them.
- What it removes. RC-10 needs no certificate of its own on route Q at any rate b0 >= 0.150314 at which the test is
  applied.

a53c946fa405b75b8950c6596f2bd88ea84174f2e1d1e43084a8d6b2056dad41, version line 23:31:28Z, by the first numerics agent) follows
theory_v15.
1. N38. Agreed as a FLOAT statement about the evaluator and as an EXPECTATION. On the compared panels (0.0269 <= r <=
   0.965, 56 percent of the FLOAT E6), the longdouble evaluator agrees with the exact enclosures to 6.9e-8 in
   aggregate, and to 4e-7 per panel for r >= 0.035. The rooms 2.49, 4.54 and 6.28 percent are rounded down, as in
   E-v14-4. Nothing in V15-0 item 2 changes: the plan of record (b0 0.55, mu 72) stands, the fallback is not
   triggered on this evidence, and (R1) stays OPEN until the certified uppers of all 561 panels and both endpoint
   records exist.
2. N38 item 4. Agreed that a comparison of a_n cannot locate the 0.15 percent discrepancy of D6(a_r) at order 6,
   because a_r - a_n = c/(1 + 4 r^2) is exactly known and radial. The rerun on the panels up to r = 8 should report:
   - the zero-mode share of E6 for a_n and for a_r separately;
   - the cross term of the zero mode of a_n with a_c, since D6(a_r)^2 = D6(a_n)^2 + 2 <D^3 a_n, D^3 a_c> + D6(a_c)^2.
   That locates the discrepancy in the one term that differs.
3. E39 and E40 are accepted; V15-7 (c) already reads E39 this way.
4. N40 (HEURISTIC timing). The near owners n0 to n2 are expected to end about 08:10Z to 08:58Z on 11-04, and n3
   about 11:30Z (numerics_v11 N35), so (R1) can be decided at the earliest after about 11:30Z. That is consistent
   with V15-0 item 5.
5. Response item 6 (the second numerics agent's band_margins.py). For the FLOAT band sample, V16-1 (b) has a bearing on the method:
   - near roots 98 to 112 the branch terms of the background are up to about 1e10 times the fields, so a binary64 sum
     of branch terms keeps at most about 6 significant digits there;
   - the absolute coefficients of branch 14's polynomial sum to about 1e353, beyond the binary64 range, while
     |P_14| is about 1e10 at t = 1, so that branch cannot be evaluated from its coefficients in binary64.
   This matters only if band_margins.py uses the branch form; an evaluation from the candidate fields, as the second numerics agent
   describes for large r, avoids it.
6. N37 and N39 (b27s, b28s) are FLOAT research items that no theory item uses; the center stays C2-N1-013.

   point), so the FLOAT margin to g_* <= 0.14215453 (beta_0* = 93/50) is 0.0037. This replaces the "about 0.004 above
   0.1378" of V9-3 (a). A sampled maximum approaches the supremum from below; the rate 93/50 needs the numerical auditor's certified
   gradient cover. With it D grows by a factor of 1.13 to 1.14 against 7/4 (V10-6 (d), V10-7 (b) 7).
3. N20 (roundoff floor and longdouble ||F_*||_2). Accepted as FLOAT, with three consequences.
   - 013. The longdouble values 7.9625e-7 (MID 32) and 7.9628e-7 (MID 40) and the second numerics agent's 7.90e-7 lie 3 percent below the
     stipulated forcing upper 8.2e-7 of V10-3 and V10-4. The f 8e-7 rows lie 0.5 percent above the larger value.
   - 009. The longdouble 2.8187e-6 and the second numerics agent's 2.7836e-6 lie above the f = 2.76e-6 of the V9-3 budgets. V10-6 (d)
     replaces those cells by direct budgets at f 2.85e-6 (also at 2.79e-6 and 2.9e-6). E31 withdraws the 2.8476e-6
     reading as accurate to its digits; the V9-3 cell at that f agrees with the new N 0.022 column.
   - A certified upper f needs an error-bounded evaluation, not a further fit. For orientation only (rounding model of
     AT-738, CONFIRMED under its hypotheses): with n = 12273 terms and sum |terms| about 4.6e9 at r = 1 (N20), the
     worst-case bound gamma_(n-1) sum |terms| for recursive summation is about 3.1e-6 per point in longdouble
     (u = 2^-64), above the field itself, and about 3.5e-9 for pairwise summation (gamma_14). The per-term errors of
     exp, log and the trigonometric factors come in addition (numerical audit exchange v163 refutes a majorant that omits them),
     and a pointwise bound still needs a quadrature or interval argument for the plane integral. Interval or exact
     rational evaluation on panels, as in the numerical auditor's annulus route, avoids both. The longdouble agreement between MID 32
     and MID 40 (to 4e-5 for 013, to 1e-5 for 009, 011 and 012) is a FLOAT consistency check, not such a bound.
   - The certified statement about the L2 residual of any candidate is still the numerical auditor's six-panel lower
     ||F_*||_2 >= 7.657e-8 for 009 (response item 6). V9-1 and V10-3 (c) need a certified lower near the FLOAT value;
     V10-4 (g) gives the permitted upper for the near test.
4. N20.4 (a) (N_2 under longdouble). The weighted E_0 parts of N_2 move by 2e-4 (P-S1) and 4e-5 (P-S2) relative
   between the binary64 and the longdouble field of 013, so the N_2 values move by less than 1e-4 relative (FLOAT).

   whole-plane N_(21/10) it stays OPEN (AT-762, V10-3 (d)).

   larger 013 value, which is the size of the difference between the two 013 runs. The N 0.006 column changes D by
   less than 1 percent against N 0.0055. For 009, N 0.022 lies above 0.021918 (V10-6 (d)). D grows by a factor of 1.33
   to 1.36 from N 0.022 to N 0.0055 at fixed f (V10-4 (g)).
6. N17 (exact far tables) and response item 3. The classes below -4.5 stay loaded at 1e8 to 1e10 and carry the P-S2

7. N18 (runs). b18s3 (longdouble 7.000e-7, not snapshotted) would raise D by a factor of about (7.96/7.00)^2 = 1.29

   (a) an error-bounded ||F_*||_2 of 013 (item 3), or the per-point error model that a certified evaluation would use;

   that theory_v08 used for 009, which came from a coarser grid. Consequence (V9-3 (a)): the rate 187/100, which needs
   g_* <= 0.13215453, is not supported at any center. The rate 93/50 needs g_* <= 0.14215453. The largest sampled
   value, 0.1378 (the second numerics agent), leaves a FLOAT margin of about 0.004 there. A sampled maximum is not an upper; it approaches

   For orientation (stipulated, AT-393): at l = 1.3e-6 the P-S1 CE levels at b0 >= 0.60 are 0.097958 to 0.137694; 012's
   mesh N_2 0.00602 is a lower for N_(21/10) only, and the ratio N_(21/10)/N_2 of about 1.6 that the second numerics agent reports for

   0.01 x 8.6e-5/3.66, about 2.4e-7, beyond r = 1e4 (sufficient only, weighted L^2 tail only; AT-433). It is not
