## Response to numerics_v04

numerics_v04 (exchange/numerical_results/numerics_v04.md, sha256
6f63bf17d51a7bd856d45217b6618854d91a10fe614ae4323886943dc3457c37, published 05:01:14Z by the first numerics agent) follows theory_v04
(ACK 03:36Z). Used here: N12.2b (the far-field-first fits), N12.3 and the plan. First reactions are in the first theory agent's note 27
(05:04Z) and note 28 (05:07Z).
1. Version reading. numerics_v04 still cites the AN-089 lowers 0.0973 and 0.0641 at P-S1 and calls the P-S1 ceilings
   CLAIMED. Since theory_v05 the transfer and the ceilings are CONFIRMED (AT-303, AT-304), the lowers are 0.231239122
   and 0.149564725 (AT-351), and every explicit route-Q test is excluded at both registered b7 centers (AT-335,
   AT-352). Plan item 3 ("the P-S1 route for 007 + h_phi") therefore applies to the new 007 center 007 + b14s
   (C2-N1-009) and not to 007 + b7.
2. Budget formula of the soft rows. The rows use budget(alpha) = 0.01 sqrt(-2 alpha - 4.8) R^(-alpha - 2.4) at
   R = 1e4. This is the P-S2 case of the sector budget rule (T2.2, "Far-field sector budgets") with the factor
   (1 + r0^2/R^2)^(sigma/2) set to 1, which changes it by less than 1e-8 at R = 1e4. The P-S1 budgets are 25 to 28
   times larger at the classes e to a8 (9.12 against 0.322 at e, 93.2 against 3.66 at a8), so rows weighted by the
   P-S2 budgets serve both tuples.
3. Plan item 2 (lattice atoms for the modes 49 to 159). For C5 + b14s the a8 circle norm 6.6, which comes from the
   high modes without lattice atoms, is 1.8 times its P-S2 budget at R = 1e4 and 7 percent of its P-S1 budget
   (93.2). By the sector rule, atoms for these modes are not needed at P-S1 at R = 1e4. theory_v07 added that at P-S2
   they are needed unless the certified annuli reach R = 1e5; AT-433 REFUTES that necessity inference. A pure a8
   sector of circle norm 33/5 with the full P-S2 weight has an exact tail upper of about 0.0090365 beyond R = 30000,
   below 0.01; this does not certify the full C5 source at that radius (AT-433). The sector rule is sufficient only.
   AT-433 also notes that the soft-row formula drops a positive weight factor and is approximate. The rule bounds the
   weighted L^2 tail only, not N_q.
4. Classes below -4.5. N12.2b states that the least squares loads them with large mutually cancelling coefficients
   (1e8 to 1e10, deeper ones to 5.6e13), and that they set the remaining mesh E_0 at 1e3 <= r <= 1e4. One complete
   sector of norm 1e8 to 1e10 at a = -4.5 has one-sector tail upper at most 0.01 beyond the sufficient radii 1.21e4
   to 7.59e4 at P-S1 and 5.4e4 to 4.84e5 at P-S2 (T2.2, "New centers"; ff_deep_v2; formula AT-391; upward radii
   AT-392, AT-413). These are not necessary radii for a finite cover, and they say nothing about the observed
   cancellation (AT-393). A certified tail needs certified annuli to radii of this order for the classes actually
   present or a remainder bound for the signed finite combination (AT-290). The b15s rows to -6.58 have smaller
   one-sector radii (158 to 432 at P-S1, 220 to 661 at P-S2, at S = 1e8 to 1e10), but they improve a certified bound
   only if the achieved coefficients or a rigorous remainder improve (AT-393).
5. 007 + b14s at P-S2. The first numerics agent's raw-mesh N_2 = 0.0852 and the second numerics agent's polar 0.05775 (04:49Z; 0.0566 of it on
   300 <= r <= 1e4) differ by a factor 1.48. Both lie below the CE levels 0.10369 to 0.145749 at its size, and they
   straddle the original-test levels 0.069675 and 0.081885 at b0 0.60 and 0.65 (P-S2 levels CONFIRMED in AT-390).
   These are stipulated comparisons of FLOAT values with necessary levels; they decide neither test for the actual
   source (AT-393). Request: reconcile the two values, and report N_3 or N_(21/10) at P-S2 on the same mesh.
   The first numerics agent 05:59Z answers the first part: the mesh value is noise-inflated beyond r of about 3000 and is withdrawn, so
   0.05775 (FLOAT) is the value to compare, and it lies below the original-test levels at b0 = 0.60 and 0.65. N_3 or
   N_(21/10) at P-S2 on the corrected mesh is still requested.
6. The G1 target (N_(21/10) at P-S2 about 0.03 or less, ||F_*||_2 about 1e-5). Under the CE test the P-S2 level at
   ||F||_2 = 1e-5 is 0.141572 at the cap (AT-307), so a target of 0.03 is a planning choice and not a necessity
   (AT-271). The binding quantity for H4 is ||F||_2: the witness budget D falls roughly like ||F||_2^(-2), so at 1e-5 it
   is about 7.6 percent of its value at 2.76e-6 (requirements item 1 (d); HEURISTIC). For route Q at P-S1 the theory
   target is a source with ||F||_2 of order 3e-6 or less and a proved upper bound C^opt(b0) <= D, with D of order 1e10
   at that size (AT-383; D is sufficient and not a lower bound for C^opt(b0), AT-396).
7. N12.3 (iv). The near-field E_2 of about 6e-3 at P-S2 for every C5 center is a contribution of about 0.077 to N_2.
   At P-S1 the C5 + b14s polar N_2 of 0.0911 is near-field dominated, so for that center the near field is the lever.
   For 007 + b14s the P-S1 near-field E_2 is 1.7e-4. The origin-cap PASS (a_0* = 10.296860 and 10.297317, margins
   above q(2c - 2) = 3.40334...) is not a background certificate, as N12.3 states. For 009, AT-386 encloses the
   complete slope in (10.297317139577998823917123, 10.297317139577998823917126) and its margin over q(2c - 2) above
   6.893976456738; it also states that no global background bound follows.
8. Requests to the first numerics agent: the exact sector table of 007 + b14s; the b15s evaluation with the class norms below -4.5 and
   the P-S1 polar N_2 and E_2; N_3 at P-S1 for both b14s sources, which the moment bracket needs for an upper of
   N_(21/10) (T2.2, "New centers"); and the P-S1 tail beyond r = 1e4 from the exact sectors, as reported for C5 + b14s

9. Inputs after numerics_v04. The second numerics agent 05:08Z: C5 + b15s regresses against b14s on 0.02 <= r <= 1e4 (requirements item

## T2. Remaining lemmas

### T2.1 T1-Lemma-LK: a Lipschitz-level gap estimate for A_k. Scoping delivered and audited; the strong form is OPEN

Reports: theory_agent_1/research/lk/LK_SCOPING_v01.md (completed 21:20Z, frozen) and its correction document
theory_agent_1/research/lk/LK_SCOPING_v02.md (SHA256 58410d034ed7...), which wins where they differ. Requested by the coordinator
20:28Z item 3(b) and 21:08Z item 2. Audit: AT-094 (21:33:38Z). Referee: the external referee lk_scope_q1 (CLAIMED).

(a) Two readings of the target statement of theory_v01 T2.1.
- Weak LK: a valid conditional route (AT-094) from the corrected AT-032 statement (T1.3), T1-Thm-O1Hq or a
  Sobolev-ball inverse, and the explicit R9 and R10 hypotheses. It gives no numerical low-tier bound with known
  constants. Its source norm at the origin is N_q(F).
- Strong LK: H_L(z) <= A S_Y(F) + C_L ||z||_2, with a Hoelder source norm S_Y that does not route the origin through
  H^q. For the true operator it needs the joint stationary origin estimate of R11, which is OPEN.

(b) Origin first jet (CONFIRMED, AT-094). At the Lipschitz level the local vertical first-jet transport coefficient at
the origin is zero: Sym DV(0) - I = diag(b - 1, 0), and (L h)_y(0) = a0 ell(h) = 0 on normalized h. This refutes a
strictly positive algebraic first-jet damping bound that uses only the source derivative at the origin. It does not
refute a global inverse estimate, an estimate with a nonlocal term or weak remainder, or an augmented condition. So no
BG-q-type pointwise matrix condition with positive origin margin exists at this level. The conditions of the route
are the list BG-L0 to BG-L5 (T5), with the AT-094 qualifications. The binding item is BG-L2, the input to the OPEN
joint origin estimate.

(c) Model transport (CONFIRMED, AT-094, for the model (T0 - 1) h = -g in the S1 class).
- Axis formula (right derivative; the left derivative agrees in the S1 class): if g_y(0) = 0 and |g_y(0, s)| <= omega(s)
  with int_0^1 omega(s)/s ds finite (Dini), then |h_y(0)| <= int_0^1 omega(s)(1/s - 1) ds + 2||g||_inf. For
  omega = A s^delta this is A/(delta(1 + delta)) + 2||g||_inf, and the order 1/delta is attained.
- Wording repair (AT-115, 22:12:39Z). With f(u) = g(0, u), [h(0, y) - f(0)]/y = int_y^infinity (f(u) - f(0)) u^(-2) du
  for y > 0, so a finite right derivative exists if and only if this improper integral converges as y decreases to 0.
  An absolute Dini modulus is sufficient, not necessary (REFUTED as necessary by a conditionally convergent S1
  example). The LK_SCOPING_v02 phrase "must carry a Dini-type modulus on the outgoing axis" is corrected accordingly.
- No estimate ||grad h||_inf <= C(||g||_(C^1) + ||h||_2) holds, even for smooth compact sources and smooth solutions
  (AT-094 family with h_y(0) >= log log(1/(2e)) - log 3; the external referee family with h_y(0) = log(1/eta)).
- What this does not say (AT-094, the external referee). The order-1/delta source-only coefficient does not force beta_L = O(delta) in
  an estimate with a delta-dependent weak remainder. the external referee (CLAIMED, checked by the first theory agent, LK_SCOPING_v02 section 2) adds:
  (i) along alpha + delta -> 0 jointly, no estimate H_L(z) <= A ||<X>^nu G||_(C^(1+alpha+delta)) + C ||z||_2 has A and
  C both bounded, for the frozen operator and for the true L with a fixed C^3 normalized background; at fixed
  alpha > 0, delta > alpha/(b - 1) is bounded below, so this is not divergence as delta -> 0. (ii) For the frozen
  operator at admissible (alpha, delta, nu), every A > 0 admits a finite, unquantified C_A (compactness).
- Reading (HEURISTIC). The derivative loss is real, but it can be carried by the remainder coefficient. The size of the
  leading coefficient alone carries no coercivity information when C_L is unrestricted. A usable strong LK needs an
  explicit pair (A, C_L).

(d) What a two-tier set must supply (for the second theory agent's T2_TT_v01).
- Sufficient condition (AT-094 CONFIRMED algebra; "certifies", not "needs"). A proved estimate
  H_L(z) <= A S_Y(F) + C_L ||z||_2 on a reference set with ||z||_2 <= R certifies the low-tier self-map if
  A S_Y(F) + C_L R <= eps_L. This is not necessary for H_L(z) <= eps_L. Likewise M_H >= N(F)/beta' is an imposed
  majorant level, not a lower bound on the solution norm.
- GN low tier. If the low tier is controlled by H_L(z) <= C R^theta' M_H^(1 - theta'), theta' = (q - 2 - alpha)/q,
  with M_H >= N(F)/beta', then necessarily N(F) R^(theta'/(1-theta')) <= beta' (eps_L/C)^(1/(1-theta')), with
  theta'/(1 - theta') = (q - 2 - alpha)/(2 + alpha) <= (q - 2)/2 < (c - 1)/2 (CONFIRMED, AT-094, as a consequence of
  these two scalar conditions only). For R >= R_floor = 0.3766893/(c + 1), the power-of-R factor obeys
  R^(-p) <= R_floor^(-(c-1)/2) = 2.2574186... (FLOAT input; 2.2576773... for R >= 0.134). This bounds that factor only.
  It does not compare constants or source norms of two methods. No "factor 2 on all improvement" statement follows.
- Weighted premise REFUTED (AT-094). For sigma > 0 no constant C gives
  ||W_sigma k||_(C^(1,alpha)) <= C ||k||_2^theta ||W_sigma k||_(H^q)^(1-theta) on normalized S1 functions. A low weight
  W_tau needs at least tau <= sigma(1 - theta). T2_TT_v01 must therefore state its low norm (unweighted, localized or
  weighted within that relation) and prove the interpolation premise for it.
- FLOAT sizes for orientation only: S1 = ||<X>^(7/4) grad F||_inf = 8.958 (007) and 1.792 (E6a), and
  S_F(007) in [112.8, 158.5] at P-H (numerics_v01 N2). Without an explicit (A, C_L) they decide nothing.
- C^(1+alpha+delta) and H^(2+alpha+delta) have the same scaling index. This is not an ordering of the norms (AT-094).

(e) Verdict. Weak LK: within reach and conditional, with N_q(F) at the origin. Strong LK for the true operator: OPEN,
needing the joint origin estimate and explicit constants. The recommendation not to pursue T1-Lemma-LK before X4 is a
scheduling judgment, not a theorem (AT-094). The outputs that matter are the confirmed model statement, the confirmed
majorant algebra and exponent cap, the refuted weighted GN premise (a constraint on T2_TT_v01), and the q-uniform
ceiling of T3.4b.

### T2.2 T1-Lemma-QWG: explicit C_eps for k = 0. OPEN; HF-NEC PROVED (AT-211); LF-1, FZ, the far-zone bound, Lemma QW and the budget PROVED (AT-212, AT-213, AT-150, AT-151); HF-Q budget for C^opt(b0) (AT-229, AT-230, AT-234 to AT-238); target X4

Statement and dependence as in theory_v01 T2.2: for BG-1, BG-2 and BG-3 at (q, sigma, r0, beta), 2 < q < 3 and
0 <= sigma < 1 + gamma_*, T1-Lemma-WG holds with an explicit C_eps = Phi(q, sigma, r0, eps; B), where B is a finite
list of named background quantities. Which finite list suffices is OPEN (AT-123 leaves the C_0 to C_3-only
dependency OPEN). Working drafts: theory_agent_1/research/qwg/QWG_v01.md (audited in AT-150 to AT-152 and AT-164) and
theory_agent_1/research/qwg/QWG_v02.md (snapshot 5ba2d4fd6caa... audited in AT-211 to AT-216; the text 4fc1a1cf7115... with the
section 6a addendum in AT-217, AT-218).

Definition (rate form; AT-215). With g = <D>^q u, h = W^(-1) u and L_W u = W L(W^(-1) u), for a real rate b,
    C^opt(b) = inf { C >= 0 : Re <<D>^q L_W u, <D>^q u> <= -b ||g||^2 + C ||h||^2 for all real S1 Schwartz u }
             = max(0, sup_(u != 0) [Re <<D>^q L_W u, <D>^q u> + b ||g||^2] / ||h||^2),
with C^opt(b) = infinity if no such C exists. C_eps^opt(eps) = C^opt(beta - eps). C^opt is non-decreasing in b and
finite for b < beta (AT-029).

HF-NEC (T1-Thm-HFNEC; PROVED, AT-211, the theory auditor research/sharp_matrix_rate_ceiling/PROOF.md).
- Hypotheses (abstract form): q > 0; W = (1 + |X|^2/r0^2)^(sigma/2) with r0 > 0, sigma >= 0; J = (1 - Delta)^(1/2),
  B_j = d_j J^(-1), R_j = d_j |D|^(-1); A, K bounded continuous real symmetric 2 x 2 fields and d a bounded continuous
  scalar, with A(PX) = P A(X) P, K(PX) = P K(X) P, d(PX) = d(X) for each coordinate reflection P; an energy form on real
  S1 Schwartz tests with the exact representation
      E(g) = q int (Bg)^T A (Bg) + int (Rg)^T K (Rg) - int d g^2 + Re <C g, g>,   C compact on L^2.
- Conclusion: with H = q A + K - d I and beta = -sup_X lambda_max H(X), if E(g) <= -b ||g||^2 + C0 ||W^(-1) J^(-q) g||^2
  for all such tests with finite C0 >= 0, then b <= beta.
- Application: for the weighted Garding decomposition of AT-029 (A = Sym DV, K = Kmat, d = c + 1 + V.grad log W, so
  H = N_q; the compact C is the retained AT-029 hypothesis with its smoothness, decay, R1 and weight assumptions,
  2 < q < 3 and 0 <= sigma < 1 + gamma), C^opt(b) = infinity for every b > beta. The endpoint b = beta is not decided.
  The statement concerns this fixed norm; for an equivalent energy norm it is OPEN.
- Proof idea (AT-211): four reflected packets sqrt(n) phi(sqrt(n)(X - X*)) cos(n omega.X) at an off-axis X*; the weak
  term is O(n^(-2q)), the compact part tends to 0, and the principal part tends to omega^T H(X*) omega.
- AT-217: N_q is covariant under the S1 reflections, although grad rho_bar is not a vector under the y reflection;
  the QWG_v02 sentence that called it one is REFUTED. HF-NEC is unaffected.

Consequences.
- (a) For unchanged 007 at P-S2: 3/5 <= beta < 0.6588409179 (P-BG4, AN-056, AT-172; AN-068, AT-199). So every rate
  b >= 0.6588409179 is impossible for the k = 0 weak inequality of 007 at P-S2, whatever the weak constant, and
  equally for Cbar^opt on any coefficient ball containing k = 0 (AT-211). Budget rows at b = 0.6607, 0.6678 or 0.6730
  are void for 007 (QWG_v02 section 6, T2_BUD_v01); they remain meaningful for a corrected center that has such a
  rate.
- (b) For every normalized background, beta <= c + 1 - q - max(q(2c - 2) - a_0,
  0) <= c + 1 - q = 0.710319210199998... (EXACT form; AT-087, AT-167; the origin yy entry of N_q is q - c - 1 < 0).
- (c) For the corrected centers C5 + h and E6a + h the BG-5 = BG-6 margins at P-S2 are 0.71027 to 0.71033 (FLOAT,
  origin-bound, no cover; the second numerics agent 23:54Z, 01:16Z). Rates up to about 0.71 are plausible there (HEURISTIC), not
  certified.
- (d) b = 0.7103 lies 1.92102e-5 below the cap c + 1 - q (the exact difference is 1.92101999998...e-5, from the cap
  0.710319210199998..., AT-266). It is an interior rate, not an endpoint (AT-215).

(w in W^(1,infinity), so that |w(x) - w(y)| <= L |x - y|; a pointwise derivative bound alone is not enough, AT-268;
the smooth radial cutoffs used here qualify) with L = ||grad w||_inf and essential support E, and let s <= s_E,
theta <= theta_E and d >= d_E on E (finite s_E, theta_E >= 0). With A_E = q(c + s_E) and b_E = d_E - A_E - theta_E,
the far part of the principal form obeys

from int w |B g|^2 <= int w |g|^2 + 3 L ||g||^2. The coefficient extrema must cover the whole support of w, including
the transition annulus. The QWG_v02 section 3 far-zone margin without the complementary theta term is not proved

  actual closed generator A0 satisfy the audited full inverse and domain hypotheses with the base weak energy
      Re (J^q[W A0 W^(-1) u], g) <= -b0 ||g||_2^2 + C0 ||h||_2^2,   b0 > 0, C0 >= 0,
  the perturbed inverse exists uniformly on the ball by the same framework, and its solution of A_k h = -F obeys
  ||h||_2 <= R. With N_F = ||J^q(WF)||_2 and Phi(M) = [b0 - L_Q(R, M)] M > 0, the exact sufficient self-map test is
      N_F <= Phi(M) - C0 R^2/M,   that is   C0 <= M (Phi(M) - N_F)/R^2.
  The squared form (Phi - N_F)^2/(b0 R^2) is a conservative sufficient test (AT-229 (5)). The base energy is the
  inequality that defines C^opt(b0) in this section, so every C0 >= C^opt(b0) may be used, and the test asks for an
  explicit upper bound of C^opt(b0) below M (Phi(M) - N_F)/R^2. HF-NEC requires b0 <= beta of the same background;
  for unchanged 007 at P-S2 the rate b0 = 3/5 is the certified lower margin, finiteness of C^opt(b0) is guaranteed
  only for b0 < beta (AT-029), and 13/20 and 7/10 are not supplied (AT-230).

Lemma QW (PROVED, AT-150). With P = chi_rho psi_mu(D) (Fourier cutoff first), kappa(mu) the weighted L^1 norm of the
kernel of psi(D/mu) <D>^q and Gamma = 2^(sigma/2) W(2 rho) kappa(mu): ||P <D>^q u|| <= Gamma ||h||, and for
C = C_s + C_P P with ||C_s|| <= tau, ||C_P|| <= A, |<C g, g>| <= (tau + eta) ||g||^2 + A^2 Gamma^2/(4 eta) ||h||^2. This
replaces the finite-rank (compactness) step of Lemma WG by an explicit constant; the factors may not be interchanged
without a commutator estimate (AT-150). Use (AT-164): with C_4 = C_s + C_P chi_rho psi_mu(D), ||C_s|| <= eps/4 and
||C_P|| <= A, the weak coefficient is A^2 2^sigma W(2 rho)^2 kappa(mu)^2/eps after spending eps/4 in Young's
inequality; a separately certified principal error eps/2 completes the slack. The missing input is an actual
decomposition of the compact remainder with certified spatial and frequency tails.

Packet remark (AT-152, with the AT-164 qualification; unchanged from theory_v03). Along the AT-152 sequence (X* fixed
with positive coordinates, carrier cos(n x), width n^(-1/2), four reflected compact bumps, n -> infinity) every fixed
compact remainder has Rayleigh quotients tending to 0; T = -<., v> v needs no weak constant (AT-152). So
W(2 rho)^2 kappa(mu)^2 is the price of the upper construction of Lemma QW, not a lower bound for C_eps^opt.

Orders (HEURISTIC; kappa FLOAT diagnostic of research/qwg/qwg_orders_v1.py, noncontaining Simpson values (AT-164); the
coefficient sizes B0, B1 and A = 1 are invented placeholders): kappa(mu) is about 5 to 85 times mu^q for 1 <= mu <= 24;
Phi is of order 4e7 to 2e12 for the three-zone organization and 6e9 to 4e23 for the plain one. This is planning
advice, not a failure statement: if the scalar surplus at a radius is s > 0, every Cbar < s^2/(b R^2) passes there
(AT-164).

Probe (QWG_v02 section 7, restated by AT-215; runs and audits in the next paragraph). A Rayleigh quotient gives a
lower bound for C^opt(b) only for admissible tests of the whole-plane operator. Admissible designs: real S1 Schwartz
tests, for example compactly supported ones with a quantified tail of the nonlocal terms; or periodic trigonometric
polynomials with a stated transfer to the plane. A test that is both compactly supported and band-limited does not
exist, so the combined design of the snapshot is withdrawn. A self-adjoint realization and a certified probe are
OPEN (AT-215).

AT-282). Periodic box [-16, 16]^2, the 007 background at P-S2, trial functions chi h with a smooth bump chi and a
finite Fourier sum h, packet scans and block eigen-solves.

  b = 0.70, with one positive value at b = 0.80. The 150-packet fine file has positive samples, and the 36-packet
  finer file is negative. Six b-specific values change sign between refinements. The packet JSON labels Gaussian

- AT-281 REFUTED the readings that theory_v04 took from the second numerics agent. Negative values on a spanning set do not make the form
  negative on the trial space. Four negative Ritz pairs can miss a positive eigenvalue, and the quoted residuals do
  not certify the spectral top. The sign changes between grids show unresolved error; they do not prove a unique
  aliasing mechanism. The second numerics agent withdrew the three sentences (03:05Z). The width below 0.02 and frequency above 500
  needed to resolve the HF-NEC growth at b = 0.70 are the second numerics agent's planning estimates, not necessary thresholds.
What stands: the saved probe gives no lower bound above 0 and no upper bound of C^opt(b0) at P-S2, for 007 or for
C5 + h. A probe gives a valid lower bound of C^opt(b) once its discretization and nonlocal-tail errors are certified.
Reproducing the HF-NEC growth at some b in (beta, 0.75] is a useful calibration, not a precondition (AT-298 (2)).
For a fitted exact center the global binding point is not proved to be the origin by sampled values (AT-298 (2)). A
probe never gives an upper bound, and the HF-Q test needs an explicit upper bound of some C0 >= C^opt(b0).

Far-field sector budgets (the first theory agent research/farfield_budget/FF_BUDGET_v04.md, SHA256 0f6d6782eeb9..., which replaces
v02 after AT-311 and AT-312 and v03 (33f4206b9d3d...) after AT-320; the rule and the exact formula are CONFIRMED as
conditional statements in AT-311, the forty rounded-down allowances, the twelve exponent threshold pairs and the
ratio displays in AT-320, and the consequences are HEURISTIC). Hypotheses: (q,
sigma, r0) is P-S2 or P-S1, W = (1 + r^2/r0^2)^(sigma/2), R > 0, and on r >= R F = sum_(k=1..K) r^(a_k)
g_k(theta) + F_rem with 2 a_k + 2 sigma + 2 < 0 and C_k = ||g_k||_(L^2(S^1)). Then
    ||W F 1_(r >= R)||_2 <= (1 + r0^2/R^2)^(sigma/2) r0^(-sigma) sum_k C_k R^(a_k+sigma+1)/sqrt(-2(a_k+sigma+1))
                           + ||W F_rem 1_(r >= R)||_2,
by Minkowski's inequality and the AT-295 upper bound for each pure power. If the g_k have pairwise disjoint angular
frequency supports, the sum may be replaced by the root of the sum of squares. The rule allocates a budget among the
sectors. A certificate also needs a proved bound of F_rem and its validity domain (AT-290, AT-302). The rule bounds
the weighted L^2 tail only. An upper bound of N_q(F) needs in addition the derivative terms, which for r^a g(theta)
are of order r^(a-1) with angular-frequency factors, and a localization of J^q. Several sectors and the remainder
share one budget. Largest circle norm C of one sector whose tail bound beyond R is at most 0.01, rounded down to
three significant digits, so that each entry is a sufficient single-sector allowance
(research/farfield_budget/ff_budget_v2.out; AT-311 found 13 of the 40 entries of the v02 table rounded upward):

Moment bracket (standard interpolation; EXACT inequalities, not a new result; CONFIRMED in AT-384, and as part of the
complete-region assembly theorem in AT-397). Let g = W F lie in H^3(R^2), g not zero, J = <D> and N_s = ||J^s g||_2.
Then N_2 <= N_(21/10) <= N_2^(9/10) N_3^(1/10), and N_(21/10) >= N_2^(11/10)/N_1^(1/10). For g = 0 all norms vanish.
Proof. N_s^2 = (2 pi)^(-2) int <xi>^(2s) |g^(xi)|^2 dxi. The first inequality holds because <xi> >= 1. For the
second, write <xi>^(21/5) |g^|^2 = (<xi>^4 |g^|^2)^(9/10) (<xi>^6 |g^|^2)^(1/10) and apply Hoelder with exponents
10/9 and 10. For the third, write <xi>^4 |g^|^2 = (<xi>^(21/5) |g^|^2)^(10/11) (<xi>^2 |g^|^2)^(1/11), apply Hoelder
with exponents 11/10 and 11, and obtain N_2^11 <= N_(21/10)^10 N_1. QED.
- Use. A certified whole-plane upper of N_(21/10) follows from certified whole-plane uppers of N_2 and N_3. The
  Hoelder upper lies below a level L exactly when N_2 < (L/N_3^(1/10))^(10/9). This is a condition on the
  interpolation upper, not a necessary condition for N_(21/10) < L (AT-385). At L = 0.131231 it reads N_2 < 0.11595,
  0.10706, 0.09696, 0.091115, 0.087009 and 0.080905 for N_3 = 0.4, 0.82, 2.0, 3.5, 5.3 and 10.2
  (research/moment_bracket/moment_bracket_v1.out, Part B; nearest decimals, not directed certificates, AT-384). The
  factor N_3^(1/10) is weak, so the certified whole-plane N_2 decides.
- Check (FLOAT). In all 44 FFT-box entries of the second numerics agent (NQfft_*.json; 40 on the box L = 64 and 4 on L = 256) the
  bracket holds, with the Hoelder upper below 1.028 times the direct value (moment_bracket_v1.out, Part A; AT-384).
  These are FLOAT observations.
- Regional monotonicity. For integer m, let nabla^m g be the tensor of all derivatives of order m and
  E_m(Omega) = ||nabla^m g||^2_(L^2(Omega)); it is nondecreasing in the region Omega. Since <xi>^4 = 1 + 2 |xi|^2 +
  |xi|^4 and |xi|^4 = sum_(i,j) xi_i^2 xi_j^2, the whole-plane N_2^2 equals E_0 + 2 E_1 + E_2 on R^2. A regional
  N_2, assembled as (E_0 + 2 E_1 + E_2)^(1/2) on Omega, is therefore a lower of the whole-plane N_2. For non-integer s
  no such statement holds, which is why AT-356 REFUTED a whole-plane bracket for N_(21/10) from regional values. A
  whole-plane upper needs complete matching disk, annulus and exterior certificates through order 3 for one common
  source (AT-381, AT-397).

### T2.7 FW-C2-HqK-RC-v1: FW-C2-HqK-v1 at a re-centered background (the coordinator 21:36Z item 2(b)). Corrected statement PROVED (AT-123); hypotheses OPEN

Re-centering identity. This is T2-RC (the second theory agent T2_O2S_v02 section 9; AT-060 CONFIRMED under explicit L^2 center and domain
conditions). Let h_* be a real S1 center and set:
- rho_* = rho_bar + h_*;
- u_* = u_bar + U[h_*];
- V_* = cX + u_* = V + U[h_*];
- F_* = F + L h_* + U[h_*].grad h_*, the full nonlinear residual of rho_*.
Then h = h_* + k solves the profile problem if and only if k solves the same problem with background (rho_*, u_*) and
source F_*:
    L_* k + U[k].grad k = -F_*,   where L_* k = V_*.grad k - k + grad rho_*.U[k].
The linear part L h_* of F_* has the sign convention of T1.1, so that L h0 = -F.

Statement (PROVED in the corrected form of AT-123, the theory auditor audit_v52, 22:22:05Z; it audited the 22:17:28Z draft of this
section). Suppose RC-1 to RC-10 below hold for h_* and for a tuple (q, sigma, r0) with 2 < q < 3. Then the full inverse
and the conditional invariant-ball implications of FW-C2-HqK-v1 (AT-069) and of AT-114 hold with these replacements:
- (rho_bar, u_bar, V, F, beta, beta_0) are replaced by (rho_*, u_*, V_*, F_*, beta*, beta_0*);
- R_* = ||F_*||_2/beta_0*;
- N(F) is replaced by N(F_*).
In particular, for epsilon in (0, betaK_*) and delta0 > 0 there is a finite Cbar, depending on rho_*, q, W, epsilon,
delta0, Rbar and Mbar and uniform over Kbar, such that the actual full L^2 inverse z = -(L_* + U[k].grad)^(-1) G obeys
    (betaK_* - epsilon) N(z) <= N(G) + (1 + delta0) N(k) ||grad z||_inf + sqrt((betaK_* - epsilon) Cbar) ||z||_2,
    ||z||_2 <= ||G||_2/beta_0*.
If (6) of AT-114 (T3.4d) holds on a normalized sub-ball with R_* <= Rbar and M <= Mbar, or (D2-K) and (D1-K) hold with
these data, R5 gives a stationary solution h = h_* + k. F_* = 0 gives h = h_* directly. This is a conditional theorem;
no sampled center is known to meet its hypotheses.

Reason for the label. AT-123 checked every hypothesis against AT-060, AT-065, AT-069 and AT-114. The transfer uses the
exact identity F + L(h_* + k) + U[h_* + k].grad(h_* + k) = F_* + L_* k + U[k].grad k, the decomposition
L_* + U[k].grad = A_(h_* + k) + U[.].grad h_* of AT-060 with a Neumann argument for the rate, and the AT-065 compact-
operator argument on the fixed new reference ball. My draft's RC-2 (three derivative orders) was REFUTED as sufficient
for BG-1 (below).

Hypotheses. The AT-060 and AT-091 conditions come first.
- RC-1 (center). The center h_* is:
  - real, S1 (even in x, odd in y) and in L^2;
  - in the graph domain of L, so that L h_* is in L^2.
  In addition, U[h_*] is bounded and globally Lipschitz, grad h_* is bounded, and g_* := ||grad h_*||_inf < beta_0.
  rho_* and u_* are smooth, and the old R1 and R2 hypotheses are retained for each coefficient h_* + k used.
  Notes:
  - Smooth bounded derivatives alone do not give an L^2 center (AT-060).
  - For a center in the campaign finite basis, L^2 and graph-domain membership follow from finite potential moment
    equalities (AT-092).
- RC-2 (BG-1 for rho_*; BG-reg; corrected per AT-123). rho_* and u_* are C^infinity, and for some gamma_h > 0 and
  EVERY multi-index j
      |D^j grad h_*(X)| + |D^j DU[h_*](X)| <= C_j^h <X>^(-gamma_h - |j|).
  In addition 0 <= sigma < 1 + gamma', with gamma' = min(gamma_*, gamma_h) and gamma_* = 1 - 1/c for 007 (AT-013).
  Then BG-1 holds for rho_* with decay rate gamma' and constants C_j* = C_j + C_j^h (triangle inequality).
  - My draft required these bounds only for j = 0 to 3. That inference is REFUTED (AT-123): a smooth normalized S1

## T3. Admissible residual threshold

### T3.1 No certified threshold

Unchanged from theory_v01 T3.1. Every sufficient closure inequality contains constants that are not explicit
(FW-C2-Hq-v1: C_eps, c_1 to c_4, c_W; FW-C2-HqK-v1: C_eps_bar, c_4', c_W; FW-C2-main-v1: C_0, c_T, eps_0, C_U). So no
closure ratio G can be computed (WORKSPACE_CONTRACTS.md section 8 (d)). What T3 gives: the exact forms of the conditions, necessary
consequences of the named criteria, and certified-input failures of those criteria for 007. None of these is a
statement about existence, and none is a necessary condition for every invariant set (AT-091, AT-094).

(AT-063, AT-072; also on ell(k) = 0, T2_REV_v01).

  whole-plane function f, q -> log ||J^q f||_2 is convex, by Hoelder's inequality for the measure |f^(xi)|^2 dxi
  applied to <xi>^(2q). Its chord slopes increase, so with N_k = ||J^k (W f)||_2
      N_2 (N_2/N_1)^(q-2) <= N_q <= N_2^(3-q) N_3^(q-2),    2 <= q <= 3.

    reproduces it to six digits). The lower end N_q >= N_2 of my 22:17Z draft is weaker.

    E_j = sum over |d| = j of (j!/d!) ||D^d (W Q)||^2 on 0.02 <= r <= 300. research/recenter/nq_bracket_v2.py recovers

### T3.4d The gradient-only criterion (6) of AT-114. Criterion PROVED (AT-114); necessary level PROVED (AT-124); evaluation HEURISTIC

the theory auditor's AT-110 to AT-114 (22:04:55Z) audit the sharp tame bound and activate it in the WG-K setting.
- Statement (AT-114, CONFIRMED as an implication under all retained background, R1/R2 and R3/R5 hypotheses):
  - Fix a reference ball Kbar = {k real S1: ||k||_2 <= Rbar, N(k) <= Mbar} with the actual full matrix margin
    betaK = -sup over k in Kbar and X of lambda_max B_q(k)(X), required positive.
  - For 0 < epsilon < betaK and delta0 > 0 there is a finite Cbar, uniform on Kbar, such that the full L^2 solution
    z = -A_k^(-1) G obeys b N(z) <= N(G) + (1 + delta0) N(k) ||grad z||_inf + sqrt(b Cbar) ||z||_2, where
    b = betaK - epsilon.
  - Conditional invariant ball: with a = N(F)/b + sqrt(Cbar/b) R and
    zeta_grad = ((1 + delta0)/b) C_grad c_W^(1-theta) R^theta M^(1-theta), theta = (q-2)/q, the inequality
    a + zeta_grad M <= M (6) gives T(K) contained in K on the normalized ball K of radii (R, M).
  - The tame value term is gone from (6). The velocity value term remains in the actual matrix B_q(k), so a separate
    matrix-loss estimate keeps it. Cbar is qualitative and radius-dependent, and betaK is not computed for any
    candidate.
- Necessary level of (6) (exact consequence of the scalar criterion (6); derived by the first theory agent, PROVED by AT-124, the theory auditor
  audit_v52, 22:22:05Z). It is necessary for this named sufficient criterion only, not for stationary existence or for
  every use of the inverse. Since a >= N(F)/b, (6) at some M > 0 needs N(F)/b <= max over M of (M - d2 M^(2-theta)),
  with d2 = ((1 + delta0)/b) C_grad c_W^(1-theta) R^theta.
  The maximum is M_*(1-theta)/(2-theta) with M_* = [(2-theta) d2]^(-q/2). So (6) needs

      N(F) <= L6 := b (1-theta)/(2-theta) [b/((2-theta)(1 + delta0) C_grad c_W^(1-theta))]^(q/2) R^(-(q-2)/2).

  - L6 increases as Cbar, delta0 and c_W decrease and as b increases. The most favorable values are Cbar = 0,
    delta0 -> 0, c_W = 1, and b at most the k = 0 margin (0 lies in Kbar), hence at most c + 1 - q for a normalized
    background. b is a rate for the whole reference ball, so a certified lower bound for some background gap is not
    automatically an upper bound for b (AT-124).
  - c_W >= 1 is PROVED for every valid multiplier constant in ||f||_(Hdot^q) <= c_W ||W f||_(H^q), also when the test
    class is restricted to smooth normalized S1 functions (AT-124, by high-frequency packets near the origin). So
    delta0 -> 0, c_W = 1 gives an upper envelope for the AT-114 near-one family.
  - With the exact AT-064 constants C_grad = B1/sqrt(2) and C*_sym = B1/4 (as in AT-124), the comparison with (NT2-F)
    at equal (b, R) is the closed form
        L6/[T_K(b) R^(-(q-2)/2)] = r(q) := 2/(q+2) [q^2/(2 sqrt(2)(q+2))]^(q/2)   (delta0 = 0, c_W = 1).
    The denominator contains R^(-(q-2)/2); my draft wrote "L6/T_K", which omits it (REFUTED as written, AT-124).
    - log r is convex, and r(q) <= r(3) < 0.2031 on the whole interval 2 <= q <= 3 (PROVED, AT-124). r(2) = 1/(4 sqrt(2)).
    - r is 0.17675 at q = 21/10, 0.17735 at 11/5 and 0.18034 at 12/5 (FLOAT; research/recenter/l6_ratio_q.py,
      out/l6_ratio_q.txt, SHA256 70ff3eced156...; r(3) = 0.2030726, research/review/at124_envelope_check.txt).
    - The AT-033 constant C_GN = 1.0059 at q = 21/10 is larger than B1/sqrt(2) = 0.6954 and would give a smaller L6.
  - At P-S1 and G_* = 1.006e-4 (nt80), L6 = 0.287 (beta_0* = 1.862) to 0.293 (c + 1); at P-S2 0.253 to 0.258.
- Uncorrected center (AT-124, PROVED for this named scalar criterion). With the certified premise R >= Rf and the
  normalized origin cap b <= c + 1 - q, (6) at the uncorrected 007 center needs
      N(F) <= Lstar(q) := r(q) N_*(q),   2 < q < c + 1,
  with N_* the T3.4b function (AT-118). log Lstar is strictly concave with a unique interior maximum:
  2.1725818496913 < q_grad < 2.1725818496915 and 0.20830658567370 < max Lstar < 0.20830658567371 (LB and UB, 512-bit
  directed arithmetic, AT-124). This improves my product-of-maxima bound 0.2031 x 1.17608 = 0.239. My FLOAT check
  reproduces both numbers (argmax 2.17258184969139, maximum 0.2083065856737; research/review/
  at124_envelope_check.py). The certified source floors are 7.08 to 176.4. At P-S1 the T3.4 ratio 8.834776 becomes at
  least 8.834776/0.17676 = 49.98 for (6), since L6 and the (NT2-F) level carry the same factor R^(-(q-2)/2)
  (arithmetic on PROVED rows; CLAIMED). None of this is an existence obstruction or a q-uniform source lower bound.
- Re-centered center: the (6) column of T3.4c for the quadratic part, and its block "Complete F_* of the computed

Frozen origin theorem (R6.3, R6.4, used as prompt statements, EXISTING_PROOFS_REFERENCE section R6 item 2):

(EXACT forms, decimals rounded.)
- kappa_ang < delta < 1 and 1 < nu < 2. sigma = 1 is valid in the Sobolev route, but it cannot be inserted as nu = 1 in
  the frozen theorem (AT-087).
- a0 > b(1 + alpha) - 1. a0 > 10 is an EXACT comparison (AN-001), so this holds for every alpha <= 3/5 in the table.
- alpha + delta is not an integer.
- sigma <= 5 - 4/c = 2.790445 (S_F finite for 007, AT-004).
- AT-101 (CONFIRMED, conditional method): the global C^(1+beta) upper method gives the S_F consequence only for
  alpha + delta < 1. P-H = (1/2, 2/5, 7/4) has alpha + delta = 9/10 and satisfies this.
- The reference tuple stays P-H while H1 is OPEN. At alpha = 1/10, kappa_ang = 0.0617, so delta = 2/5 remains
  admissible (the coordinator 20:28Z item 3(d)).
- Joint small-loss limit (AT-116, CONFIRMED 22:12:39Z). For the frozen operator, and for the full operator on any fixed
  locally C^3 background, there is no family of estimates
  ||z||_(C^(1,alpha)) <= A(alpha, delta) ||<X>^nu G||_(C^(1+alpha+delta)) + C(alpha, delta) ||z||_2 with A and C both
  bounded as alpha + delta tends to 0 through admissible parameters (for example alpha = delta = eps/2). Growth of A
  alone does not follow.
- Fixed triple (AT-117, CONFIRMED for the frozen operator). At each fixed admissible (alpha, delta, nu), every leading
  coefficient A > 0 is possible with a finite, unquantified weak coefficient C_A. The full variable-coefficient lifting
  and effective (A, C) pairs are OPEN.
- Consequence for the parameter choice (HEURISTIC). Taking alpha and delta jointly small cannot keep both constants
  bounded, so the Hoelder route should be run at a fixed triple away from 0, such as P-H, where the decision rests on
  the explicit weak coefficient (Q-WG, T2.2).

Two-tier ball (the second theory agent T2_TT_v01; T2.6):
- The low tier is H(k) <= eps_L at the C^(1,alpha) level with alpha > 0. A C^1 low tier is not enough (AT-103).
- Strain conversion (AT-104, AT-142): for the unweighted norm h(k) = ||k||_inf + ||grad k||_inf + J_c(k),
  ||Sym DU[k]||_(inf,op) <= D_sym(alpha) h(k) with D_sym(alpha) = max(1/2, 2 sqrt(2)/(pi alpha), (8 + B)/(sqrt(2) pi)),
  B = 4(2 sqrt(2) - 1)/3; at alpha = 1/10, D_sym = 20 sqrt(2)/pi = 9.00316 (FLOAT value of an EXACT form). For the
  product-weighted H of the two-tier ball, h(k) <= C_sigma H(k), so the proved constant is D_weighted = D_sym C_sigma,
  with the EXACT safe factors C_1 = 27/4 and C_(7/5) = 919/100 (AT-142). theory_v02 used D_sym for the weighted norm;
  that attribution is REFUTED (AT-142), and a smaller weighted constant is OPEN. The strain term q D_weighted eps_L of
  the low tier must stay below beta for this bound to be useful. At q = 21/10 and beta = 3/5 a sufficient restriction
  is eps_L < pi/(70 sqrt(2) C_sigma) (AT-142 (2)): 0.004701 at sigma = 1 (P-S1, P-BG3) and 0.003453 at sigma = 7/5
  (P-S2) (FLOAT values of EXACT forms). Unweighted, the threshold pi/(70 sqrt(2)) exceeds 0.03172, so eps_L < 0.0317
  is a rounded-down sufficient restriction and not a necessary one. No bound on the actual optimal inverse radius
  follows from this sufficient strain bound. Smaller alpha raises D_sym like 1/alpha. So alpha = 1/10 is not free for
  the two-tier route.

  L_R = sup over |X| >= R of ||DV||_op.
- At (sigma_9, alpha) = (7/4, 1/2): mu_R = -0.068, 0.346 and 0.637 at R = 4, 8 and 16 (FLOAT). It is positive from R of
  about 4.6, with limit mu_infty = 1.4526 (AT-002).
- Perturbed background (BG-L4; exact under the AT-094 constant choices, CONFIRMED): mu_R(k) >= mu_R - (sigma + 1 + alpha) d
  with d = ||DU[k]||_(op,inf). For h0, d = 0.084 (FLOAT, the second numerics agent), so the loss at (7/4, 1/2) is 3.25 d = 0.273. That
  moves the FLOAT positivity radius from about 4.6 to between 4 and 8.
- C_9 and C_9' are not given by the asymptotic coefficients 2.523 and 27.914. Those fix angular limits only (AT-087).
- No finite-radius value is certified.

## T6. Sensitivity and ranked candidate changes

### T6.1 Sensitivity (HEURISTIC, from T3.4, T3.4b, T3.4c and T3.5)

- Uncorrected center. T3.4 (PROVED) excludes the coarse criterion at all ten certified tuples, by factors of at least
  8.83. The q-uniform ceiling of T3.4b (PROVED) needs N(F) < 1.17608 for the 007 residual size (AT-118), against
  certified source floors of 7.08 to 176.4. The gradient-only criterion (6) needs N(F) < 0.20830658567371 there for
  every q (UB; AT-124, T3.4d).
- Residual size. For the coarse criterion the ceiling grows only like G^(-p) with p <= (c - 1)/2 = 0.40516. Reducing
  norm F in L^2 alone cannot compensate a large strong norm.
- Re-centered center (T3.4c, T3.4d; the second numerics agent production 600 x 80 FLOAT diagnostics, AN-044 scope; ranges over the
  log-convexity bracket for N_q):
  - the binding quantity is N(F_*), not norm F_* in L^2: a factor 6.0 in G_* changes the ratios by a factor 1.09;
  - (NT2-F) holds at P-S1 with ratio 0.19 to 0.23, so it is not the binding test on these inputs;
  - T2-CF with the most favorable placeholders needs N_(21/10)(F_*) to fall by a factor 2.5 to 3.0;
  - (6) with its most favorable constants fails at P-S1 (ratio 1.10 to 1.30) and is borderline at P-S2 (0.94 to 1.13);
    P-S2 gains the factor 0.86 because N_q(P-S2)/N_q(P-S1) = 0.76 is below the break-even 0.881 (T4.1);
  - N_1, N_2, N_3 agree to 0.6 percent between the two radial methods and were stable from 80 to 96 angular nodes;
  - the complete F_* of the second numerics agent's converged grid center (22:44Z) is its discretization defect. Its N_2 (1.157 at P-S1,
    0.932 at P-S2, 600 x 80) is five times that of Q, and (6) fails there by factors of at least 4.32 (P-S1) and 3.95
    (P-S2) with c_W = 1, and 8.32 at P-S1 with the AT-135 constant c_W = 1.927. N_2 falls like ds^2 under radial
    refinement, so the discretization, not the quadratic part, is the present limitation (T3.4c).
- q. At the uncorrected center the ceiling peaks at q = 2.1706 (T3.4b). At the re-centered center the q choice for (6)
  turns on N_(11/5)(F_*)/N_(21/10)(F_*), which the bracket limits to [1.408, 1.591] at (1, 1/2), against the
  break-even 1.43 to 1.59; q = 12/5 is worse at both weights for every profile in the bracket (T3.4c reading 4).
- beta enters with power 1 + q/2 (2.05 at q = 21/10). It is capped by c + 1 - q at the origin and by
  1 + c(1 + sigma - q) at infinity. At rho_bar + h_0, the second numerics agent's BG-6 values at the three origin-bound tuples lie 0.03 to
  0.04 below the k = 0 caps (T3.4c reading 7). At P-S1 that costs a factor 1.094 in every level.
- Constants. In T2-CF, c_4' binds through the tame term; in (6) the tame coefficient is 1 + delta0 and the value term
  is gone. C_eps_bar and Cbar enter only through a term multiplied by R_* (3.6e-5 to 3.2e-4), so at the re-centered
  center they matter only if they are large (T3.4c reading 9). Their actual sizes are OPEN (AT-107, AT-114).

## Norm registry

NORM-T-HqW-v1 (weighted Bessel potential norm). Unchanged from theory_v01 except for the named tuples.
- Formula: N_(q,sigma,r0)(f) := ||<D>^q (W f)||_2, where:
  - <D>^q is the Fourier multiplier (1 + |xi|^2)^(q/2);
  - W(X) = (1 + |X|^2/r0^2)^(sigma/2);
  - the L^2 norm is the full-plane norm (WORKSPACE_CONTRACTS.md section 4).
- Parameters: 2 < q < 3, sigma >= 0 and r0 > 0, stated with every value.
- Named tuples:
  - P-Q1 = (13/5, 7/5, 1/4) and P-Q2 = (12/5, 1, 1/4);
  - P-BG1 = (13/5, 7/5, 1/4), P-BG2 = (5/2, 7/5, 1/2) and P-BG3 = P-S1 = (21/10, 1, 1/2), with the BG-3 targets 1/10,
    1/4 and 3/5;
  - P-S2 = (21/10, 7/5, 1), a reporting tuple so far, recommended here as the primary tuple of FW-C2-HqK-RC-v1 (T4.1).
- Region: R^2.
- Mandatory components:
  - E_j = ||D^j (W f)||_2 for j = 0 to 3, in the ordered-tuple Frobenius convention;
  - N_2 = (E_0^2 + 2 E_1^2 + E_2^2)^(1/2) and N_3 = (E_0^2 + 3 E_1^2 + 3 E_2^2 + E_3^2)^(1/2), which are exact for
    ||<D>^m (W f)||_2 with m = 2, 3;
  - the bracket N_2 (N_2/N_1)^(q-2) <= N_q <= N_2^(3-q) N_3^(q-2) for 2 <= q <= 3, and N_q >= N_2 (N_2/N_0)^((q-2)/2),
    for one whole-plane function (log-convexity of q -> log N_q by Hoelder in Fourier variables; CLAIMED, elementary;
    the upper end is the earlier exact interpolation bound). N_1 = (E_0^2 + E_1^2)^(1/2);
  - the method, radial range, far-field treatment and label.
- Conversion (AT-057): ||D^2 f||_2 <= C_inv N_q(f) with C_inv = (1 + 2 C1^2 + C2^2)^(1/2), C1 = sigma/(2 r0) and
  C2 = (sqrt(2) sigma + sigma^2/4)/r0^2.
- Users:
  - FW-C2-O1Hq-v1, as the source and solution norm;
  - FW-C2-Hq-v1, FW-C2-HqK-v1 and FW-C2-HqK-RC-v1, as the ball norm N(k) <= M and the source norm (N(F), or N(F_*) at
    a re-centered background).
- Not comparable with NORM-SF or NORM-H without a cited conversion. The one stated conversion is
  H_(sigma,alpha)(f) <= c_mu C_S N_(q,sigma,r0)(f) for 0 < alpha <= q - 2 (T1.2).
- Values of different (q, sigma, r0) are different norms. T3.4c compares each N_q(F_*) only with the level at the same
  tuple.

  (E6a) RC-2, the qualitative part of RC-1 and RC-4 are PROVED (AT-162), and every quantitative hypothesis (g_*, RC-3,
